Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

For a realization as in [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], set $Q=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ and $Q^+=\bigoplus_{i=1}^n\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Define $\operatorname{ht}(\sum_i k_i\alpha_i)=\sum_i k_i$. For $\lambda,\mu\in\mathfrak h^*$ write $\mu\le\lambda$ if $\lambda-\mu\in Q^+$.

Independence of the simple roots makes coordinates unique. Thus $Q^+\cap(-Q^+)=\{0\}$, which proves antisymmetry of the order; closure under addition proves transitivity, and $0\in Q^+$ proves reflexivity. Positive roots will belong to $Q^+\setminus\{0\}$, not all of $Q^+$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves
$I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ and descends to $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. All three are
involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

derivations.claim: For each word $w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$ define $Q_w,R_w\in U_q^-$ by recursion on $m$: for the empty word $Q_1:=R_1:=0$, and for $m\ge1$, with $w'=F_{j_2}\cdots F_{j_m}$, set $Q_w:=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$ and $R_w:=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w'$. Each is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of words. If $w$ has degree $-\nu$, every nonzero term of $Q_w,R_w$ has degree $-\nu+\alpha_i$: inductively a nonzero $Q_{w'},R_{w'}$ has degree $\deg w'+\alpha_i$, multiplication by $F_{j_1}$ gives $\deg w+\alpha_i$, and the term $\delta_{ij_1}w'$ has that degree when $j_1=i$.

For every word $w$ one has $E_iw-wE_i=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. For $m=0$ both sides vanish. For $m\ge1$, write $w=F_{j_1}w'$. Multiplying the inductive identity for $w'$ by $F_{j_1}$ on the left gives $F_{j_1}E_iw'=F_{j_1}w'E_i+F_{j_1}K_iQ_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})-F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}R_{w'}/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, and [F3] gives $E_iF_{j_1}-F_{j_1}E_i=\delta_{ij_1}(K_i-K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Adding, and using [F2] in the form $F_{j_1}K_i=q_i^{a_{ij_1}}K_iF_{j_1}$, $F_{j_1}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}K_i^{-1}F_{j_1}$, yields $E_iw-wE_i=\bigl(K_i(q_i^{a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}Q_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')-K_i^{-1}(q_i^{-a_{ij_1}}F_{j_1}R_{w'}+\delta_{ij_1}w')\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})=(K_iQ_w-K_i^{-1}R_w)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, which is the claim.

Existence follows for every $P\in U_q^-$: by [F1] write $P=\sum_wc_ww$ as a finite linear combination of words, and set $Q:=\sum_wc_wQ_w$, $R:=\sum_wc_wR_w$. Summing the identities of step 2.1 with coefficients $c_w$ gives $E_iP-PE_i=(K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$.

Consequently $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are well defined on all of $U_q^-$; they are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear because the defining identity is linear in $P$: if $P=c_1P_1+c_2P_2$, the pairs $(c_1Q(P_1)+c_2Q(P_2),\,c_1R(P_1)+c_2R(P_2))$ satisfy the defining identity for $P$, so by uniqueness each map is linear. The recursion gives $Q_1=R_1=0$, hence $e_i'(1)=e_i''(1)=0$; and for the one-letter word $w=F_j$ the recursion gives $Q_{F_j}=R_{F_j}=\delta_{ij}$, hence $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$.

For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$ decompose $E_i(xy)-(xy)E_i=(E_ix-xE_i)y+x(E_iy-yE_i)$ and substitute the defining identities for $x$ and $y$: the right side equals $\bigl(K_ie_i''(x)y-K_i^{-1}e_i'(x)y+xK_ie_i''(y)-xK_i^{-1}e_i'(y)\bigr)/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. By [F2] with $\operatorname{wt}(x)$ in place of $\beta$, $xK_i=K_iq_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$ and $xK_i^{-1}=K_i^{-1}q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x$. Collecting the $K_i$- and $K_i^{-1}$-coefficients and using the uniqueness of step 4.1 yields the two twisted Leibniz rules of (b).

Grading and nilpotence. The degree computation of step 1.1 shows that for a word $w$ of degree $-
u$, every nonzero term of $Q_w,R_w$ has degree $-
u+\alpha_i$. These are negative words, so both coefficients vanish if $
u-\alpha_i
otin Q_+$; otherwise they belong to $U_q^-[-(
u-\alpha_i)]$. By linearity the same holds on every homogeneous component. Thus $e_i',e_i''$ raise actual degree by $\alpha_i$ and lower positive height by one, and their $k$-th powers vanish on degree $-
u$ for $k>\operatorname{ht}(
u)$. Every vector has finite homogeneous support, so both maps are locally nilpotent.

The commutation relations of (c) are the case $x=F_j$ of the Leibniz rules: $\operatorname{wt}(F_j)=-\alpha_j$, so $q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}$ and $q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(F_j),h_i\rangle}=q_i^{a_{ij}}$, while $e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ by step 5.1. Reading the resulting identities $e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ and $e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y$ as operator identities gives (c).

For the bar relation, apply the semilinear algebra automorphism $\psi$ of [F4] to the defining identity of $P$: since $\psi(E_i)=E_i$, $\psi(K_i)=K_i^{-1}$ and $\psi(q_i-q_i^{-1})=-(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, one gets $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_i\psi(e_i'(P))-K_i^{-1}\psi(e_i''(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$. Comparing with the defining identity for $\psi(P)$, namely $E_i\psi(P)-\psi(P)E_i=(K_ie_i''(\psi(P))-K_i^{-1}e_i'(\psi(P)))/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, uniqueness (step 4.1) gives $e_i''(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i'(P))$ and $e_i'(\psi(P))=\psi(e_i''(P))$. Applying the second identity to $\psi(P)$ in place of $P$ and using $\psi^2=\mathrm{id}$ gives $e_i''(P)=\psi(e_i'(\psi(P)))$, that is, $e_i''=\psi e_i'\psi$. This proves (a)–(e) and completes the definition.

boundaries.evidence: step 1.1 starts the word recursion at Q_1:=R_1:=0, and step 2.1 records that both sides of the defining identity vanish at the empty word, so e_i'(1)=e_i''(1)=0.
Linearity in step 5.1 gives e_i'(0)=e_i''(0)=0; step 4.1 proves uniqueness of zero toral coefficients.
Step 5.1 evaluates the one-letter word F_j as e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=delta_ij; step 1.1 provides its empty-word base.

the vanishing-target case nu-alpha_i not in Q_+ is step 6.1, where the recursion gives Q_w=R_w=0; uniqueness never divides by q_i^2-1 because step 4.1 separates the K_i and K_i^{-1} components linearly.
the recursion has the endpoint m=0 at the empty word (step 1.1) and terminates by the height drop of step 6.1; no other integer bound occurs in the construction.

boundaries.reason: the maps are defined by a deterministic recursion on words, and uniqueness in step 4.1 uses only linear independence of the toral elements; no choice function is invoked.
this is a uniqueness-based construction rather than a biconditional; the one derived statement e_i''=psi e_i' psi is an identity proved in step 7.1, not one direction of an equivalence.
existence (step 3.1) and uniqueness (step 4.1) are two assertions about one and the same construction, so there is no converse implication to test.

risk_review.notes: Accepted the reader's corrected commutator and toral multiplication. Read Definition and Verification 1.1–7.1 and exact dependency interfaces (DJ presentation, half grading, quantum integers, triangular decomposition, Chevalley involutions, root height). Word recursion produces coefficients in the actual quotient; independence of 1 and K_i^2 follows from nonzero independent h_i and the toral basis, so uniqueness supplies descent and linearity. Prefix crossings have opposite signs for e_i' and e_i'', actual wt(F_j)=-alpha_j; empty word, zero, one-letter and vanishing degree are covered. Bar swaps the coefficients and reverses the denominator. JKK §6 (6.1)–(6.3), printed p.22, agrees with this convention. No AC is needed for triangular decomposition (i)–(ii).

Let $\mathbb Z[t]$ be the polynomial ring over the integers
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[thm-polynomial-ring-is-a-commutative-ring]]) and let
$$S=\{t^k:k\ge0\}.$$
The set $S$ is multiplicative, and the **Laurent polynomial ring** is the
principal localisation
$$\Lambda_1:=\mathbb Z[t]_S=S^{-1}\mathbb Z[t]$$
([[def-principal-localisation]], [[def-multiplicative-subset-and-localisation]]).
It is a commutative ring with unit $1=t^0$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]). Write
again $t$ for the image of the indeterminate under the localisation map; then
$t$ is a unit with inverse $t^{-1}$
([[prop-units-in-a-localisation]]). Every element of $\Lambda_1$ has a
representative
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k,\qquad a_k\in\mathbb Z,$$
with only finitely many nonzero coefficients, obtained by writing a fraction
$p/t^N$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of the powers
$t^{k-N}$; the finite coefficient sequence is unique: after multiplying two such sums
by a common sufficiently large power of $t$, equality becomes equality of
ordinary polynomials. The localisation map $\mathbb Z[t]\to\Lambda_1$ is
injective because $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain; hence their coefficients agree
([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]]). Equivalently, two such
sums are equal exactly when their coefficient sequences agree
([[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]).

**Universal property.** Let $A$ be a ring with unit and let
$\varphi\colon\mathbb Z[t]\to A$ be a unital ring homomorphism with
$\varphi(t)$ a unit of $A$. Then there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\widetilde\varphi\colon\Lambda_1\to A$ with
$\widetilde\varphi(t)=\varphi(t)$. Equivalently, for every unital ring $A$ and
every unit $u\in A$ there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\Lambda_1\to A$ with $t\mapsto u$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]],
[[def-ring-homomorphism]]).

The cited localisation theorem treats commutative target rings. For the
possibly noncommutative target used here, define
$\sum_k a_kt^k\mapsto\sum_k(a_k1_A)u^k$. Unique Laurent coefficients make
this well defined. Integer multiples of $1_A$ are central, and
$u^ku^l=u^{k+l}$ for all integers $k,l$, so finite distributivity proves
additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. Every unital
homomorphism must send $a_k$ to $a_k1_A$ and $t^k$ to $u^k$, proving
uniqueness. Taking $u=\varphi(t)$ gives the asserted extension of $\varphi$.

**Augmentation.** There is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$$\varepsilon\colon\Lambda_1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \varepsilon\Bigl(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k\Bigr)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k,$$
the **sum-of-coefficients map** ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]]); it
is well defined because the coefficients are summable and their total sum is
unchanged along the relation of
[[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]. Its kernel is the
principal ideal $(t-1)$: indeed $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$, and if
$\varepsilon(x)=0$ then, writing $x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k$ with finite
support and using that $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k=0$, one has
$$x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k(t^k-1)=(t-1)\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k\,(1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}),$$
where $1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}$ denotes the empty sum $0$ for $k=0$ and, for
$k=-j<0$, the negative sum
$-(t^{-1}+t^{-2}+\cdots+t^{-j})$, so that
$t^{-j}-1=-(t-1)(t^{-1}+\cdots+t^{-j})$; hence $x\in(t-1)$, and the reverse
inclusion is $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$.

**Caveats.** This item realises $\Lambda_1$ by localisation and does **not**
identify it with an integral group ring: the additive group underlying
$\Lambda_1$ is $\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z\,t^k$ and its multiplication
is the polynomial one ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]] is not
needed for the ring laws but records that $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain). The
deck-module structures on homology introduced later on this page are defined
separately, by the universal property above.

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $\mathbb Z[t]$ be the polynomial ring over the integers
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[thm-polynomial-ring-is-a-commutative-ring]]) and let
$$S=\{t^k:k\ge0\}.$$
The set $S$ is multiplicative, and the **Laurent polynomial ring** is the
principal localisation
$$\Lambda_1:=\mathbb Z[t]_S=S^{-1}\mathbb Z[t]$$
([[def-principal-localisation]], [[def-multiplicative-subset-and-localisation]]).
It is a commutative ring with unit $1=t^0$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]). Write
again $t$ for the image of the indeterminate under the localisation map; then
$t$ is a unit with inverse $t^{-1}$
([[prop-units-in-a-localisation]]). Every element of $\Lambda_1$ has a
representative
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k,\qquad a_k\in\mathbb Z,$$
with only finitely many nonzero coefficients, obtained by writing a fraction
$p/t^N$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of the powers
$t^{k-N}$; the finite coefficient sequence is unique: after multiplying two such sums
by a common sufficiently large power of $t$, equality becomes equality of
ordinary polynomials. The localisation map $\mathbb Z[t]\to\Lambda_1$ is
injective because $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain; hence their coefficients agree
([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]]). Equivalently, two such
sums are equal exactly when their coefficient sequences agree
([[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]).

**Universal property.** Let $A$ be a ring with unit and let
$\varphi\colon\mathbb Z[t]\to A$ be a unital ring homomorphism with
$\varphi(t)$ a unit of $A$. Then there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\widetilde\varphi\colon\Lambda_1\to A$ with
$\widetilde\varphi(t)=\varphi(t)$. Equivalently, for every unital ring $A$ and
every unit $u\in A$ there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\Lambda_1\to A$ with $t\mapsto u$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]],
[[def-ring-homomorphism]]).

The cited localisation theorem treats commutative target rings. For the
possibly noncommutative target used here, define
$\sum_k a_kt^k\mapsto\sum_k(a_k1_A)u^k$. Unique Laurent coefficients make
this well defined. Integer multiples of $1_A$ are central, and
$u^ku^l=u^{k+l}$ for all integers $k,l$, so finite distributivity proves
additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. Every unital
homomorphism must send $a_k$ to $a_k1_A$ and $t^k$ to $u^k$, proving
uniqueness. Taking $u=\varphi(t)$ gives the asserted extension of $\varphi$.

**Augmentation.** There is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$$\varepsilon\colon\Lambda_1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \varepsilon\Bigl(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k\Bigr)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k,$$
the **sum-of-coefficients map** ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]]); it
is well defined because the coefficients are summable and their total sum is
unchanged along the relation of
[[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]. Its kernel is the
principal ideal $(t-1)$: indeed $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$, and if
$\varepsilon(x)=0$ then, writing $x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k$ with finite
support and using that $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k=0$, one has
$$x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k(t^k-1)=(t-1)\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k\,(1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}),$$
where $1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}$ denotes the empty sum $0$ for $k=0$ and, for
$k=-j<0$, the negative sum
$-(t^{-1}+t^{-2}+\cdots+t^{-j})$, so that
$t^{-j}-1=-(t-1)(t^{-1}+\cdots+t^{-j})$; hence $x\in(t-1)$, and the reverse
inclusion is $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$.

**Caveats.** This item realises $\Lambda_1$ by localisation and does **not**
identify it with an integral group ring: the additive group underlying
$\Lambda_1$ is $\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z\,t^k$ and its multiplication
is the polynomial one ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]] is not
needed for the ring laws but records that $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain). The
deck-module structures on homology introduced later on this page are defined
separately, by the universal property above.

derivations.claim: The assignment $t\mapsto q$ defines a unital ring homomorphism $\Lambda_1\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by the universal property of [F1], since $q$ is a unit of the field $\mathbb Q(q)$. It is injective: if $\sum_ka_kq^k=0$ with finitely many $a_k\ne0$, choose $N\ge0$ so that every $k+N\ge0$; then the polynomial $\sum_ka_kT^{k+N}\in\mathbb Q[T]$ vanishes at the indeterminate $q$, so by [F2] it is the zero polynomial and all $a_k=0$. Hence its image $A$ is a subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$, and in particular $A$ is a commutative domain.

Each factor $N_{i,c,s}:=K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of the toral elements $K_{d_ih_i}$ and $K_{-d_ih_i}$, and the denominator $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}=q_i^{\,-s}(q_i^{\,2s}-1)$ is nonzero for $s\ge1$: $q_i^{\,2s}=1$ would make the indeterminate $q$ a root of the nonzero polynomial $T^{2d_is}-1$ by [F2]. Hence every factor, and therefore $T_{i,c,t}$, is a well-defined element of $U_q^0$; expanding the product and using $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ and $K_iK_i^{-1}=1$ of [F3], each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a finite $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear combination of the toral elements $K_{md_ih_i}$ ($m\in\mathbb Z$), that is, a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$. Since $U_q^0$ is commutative by [F3], all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with every $K_h$ and with one another.

The listed generators are homogeneous for the root grading of [F3]: $E_i^{(r)}=E_i^r/[r]_i!$ has degree $r\alpha_i$ because $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$ and the grading is multiplicative with $[r]_i!\ne0$ by [F4]; likewise $F_i^{(r)}$ has degree $-r\alpha_i$; and $K_h^{\pm1}$ and, by step 2.1, $T_{i,c,t}$ have degree $0$.

By definition $U_A$ consists of the finite $A$-linear combinations of finite products of the listed generators, the empty product $1$ included. Every finite product of homogeneous elements is homogeneous of the sum of their degrees (the grading of [F3] is multiplicative), so every element of $U_A$ is a finite sum of homogeneous elements of $U_A$. Since $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_\beta U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ is a direct sum, this decomposition is unique, so $U_A=\bigoplus_\beta U_A[\beta]$ with $U_A[\beta]=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$; the same argument applies to the generated $A$-subalgebras $U_A^\pm$ (generators of degrees $\pm r\alpha_i$) and $U_A^0$ (degree-$0$ generators), which are therefore graded in the same way. Each $U_A[\beta]$, being the intersection of the $A$-submodule $U_A$ with a $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspace, is an $A$-submodule.

Since $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ by [F4] and the $K_h$ are among the listed generators, $U_A$ contains $E_i$, $F_i$ and $K_h$; consequently its $\mathbb Q(q)$-span contains all generators of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, so by [F5] the $\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The canonical multiplication map $\Phi\colon U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\to U_q(\mathfrak g)$, $\sum_iu_i\otimes s_i\mapsto\sum_is_iu_i$ is surjective by step 5.1. It is injective by the argument of [F6]: given $\sum_iu_i\otimes s_i$ with $s_i=a_id^{-1}$, $a_i\in A$, $0\ne d\in A$, one has $\sum_iu_i\otimes s_i=\bigl(\sum_ia_iu_i\bigr)\otimes d^{-1}$, and $\Phi(\sum_iu_i\otimes s_i)=d^{-1}\sum_ia_iu_i=0$ forces $\sum_ia_iu_i=0$ in the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $d\ne0$; hence $\sum_iu_i\otimes s_i=0$. Thus $\Phi$ is an isomorphism, which is claim (iii).

Finally, $A$ is not a principal ideal domain: the ideal $I=(2,q-1)\subseteq A$ is proper, since a relation $1=2a+(q-1)b$ would give $1=2\varepsilon(a)$ under the ring homomorphism $\varepsilon\colon A\to\mathbb Z$ with $q\mapsto1$ of [F1], in which $2a$ contributes an even integer. If $I=(d)$ were principal, then from $d\mid2$ and the domain $A$ one gets $2=de$, and reducing modulo the ring homomorphism $A\to\mathbb F_2[q,q^{-1}]$, $q\mapsto q$ (again [F1]) gives $0=\bar d\,\bar e$; if $\bar d=0$ then $q-1=df$ reduces to $q+1=0$, a contradiction, so $\bar d\ne0$ and hence $\bar e=0$, that is, $e=2e'$ for some $e'\in A$. Then $2=2de'$ and therefore $de'=1$ because $A$ is a domain with $2\ne0$, so $d$ is a unit and $1\in I$, contradicting the properness of $I$. Hence no principal ideal equals $I$. This is why no freeness, independence or triangularity statement is attached to $U_A$ in this definition; those are separate theorems with their own hypotheses.

derivations.claim: The structural conditions are mutually consistent. If $v\in M_\mu$, then by [F1] $K_h(E_iv)=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_hv=q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}E_iv=q^{\langle\mu+\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iv$, so the prescribed containment $E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ agrees with the scalar prescription on $M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$; similarly $K_h(F_iv)=q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}F_iv=q^{\langle\mu-\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iv$. Moreover $K_0$ acts on $M_\mu$ by $q^{\langle\mu,0\rangle}=1$ and $K_hK_{h'}$ by $q^{\langle\mu,h+h'\rangle}=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}q^{\langle\mu,h'\rangle}$ by [F2], as the toral relations require.
The grading-preserving module maps of the definition form a category: identities preserve each $M_\mu$, and a composite of grading-preserving maps is grading-preserving.

For $\mu\in P$ define its toral character $\chi_\mu\colon P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Q(q)^{\times}$ by $\chi_\mu(h):=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$; the defining condition says that $K_h$ acts on $M_\mu$ by the scalar $\chi_\mu(h)$. Since $M$ is the internal direct sum of the $M_\mu$, the simultaneous eigenspace $M^\chi=\{v:K_hv=\chi(h)v\ \text{for all }h\}$ is $M^\chi=\bigoplus_{\mu:\chi_\mu=\chi}M_\mu$. Two labels have the same character, $\chi_\mu=\chi_{\mu'}$, if and only if $\langle\mu-\mu',h\rangle=0$ for all $h\in P^{\vee}$; by [F3] this is exactly equality of the integer functions $h\mapsto\langle\cdot,h\rangle$. If the pairing separates $P$ (that is, $\mu\ne\mu'$ implies $\langle\mu-\mu',h\rangle\ne0$ for some $h$), each $M^\chi$ equals a single label space $M_\mu$; if it does not separate, $M^\chi$ is the sum of all label spaces sharing the character. For an explicit nonseparating witness, take $P=\mathbb Z^2$, $P^{\vee}=\mathbb Z h$, $\alpha_1=(2,0)$, $h_1=h$, $d_1=1$, with $\langle(a,b),h\rangle=a$: the distinct labels $(0,0)$ and $(0,1)$ have the same character, so a spectral eigenspace can merge two label spaces.

Kernels, images and quotients inherit gradings. For a grading-preserving $f\colon M\to N$, the restriction $f_\mu:=f|_{M_\mu}$ maps $M_\mu$ into $N_\mu$, and $\ker f=\bigoplus_\mu\ker f_\mu$, $\operatorname{im}f=\bigoplus_\mu\operatorname{im}f_\mu$ by [F4]; for a graded submodule $L\subseteq M$ (one with $L=\bigoplus_\mu(L\cap M_\mu)$) the quotient has $M/L=\bigoplus_\mu (M_\mu+L)/L$. Hence the weight submodules and quotients used on this page carry induced label gradings, and the category is closed under the usual linear algebra of grading-preserving maps. The zero module has the empty grading $M_\mu=0$ for all $\mu$.

Integrability is exactly local nilpotence of the two families of generators on each vector: it is inherited by grading-preserving submodules and quotients, since $E_i^{N}v=0$ in $M$ implies $E_i^Nw=0$ for $w$ in a submodule and $E_i^N(w+L)=0$ in a quotient; no uniform exponent and no finite dimension is required. The zero module is integrable: its only vector is $0$, and $E_i^1 0=F_i^1 0=0$, so the exponents $N_e(0,i)=N_f(0,i)=1$ witness the condition. Finite-dimensionality of the $M_\mu$ and boundedness of the support are not part of the definition and are not implied by it: for any datum, the direct sum of countably many trivial modules concentrated at label $0$ is integrable and has an infinite-dimensional label space. Unbounded support is possible for the rank-one datum $P=\mathbb Z\omega$, $\alpha=2\omega$, $P^\vee=\mathbb Zh$, $\langle\omega,h\rangle=1$: the direct sum of the finite strings $L(n)$, $n\ge0$, is integrable (each vector occupies finitely many summands) and has arbitrarily high labels, by [[thm-quantized-sl-two-string-formulas]](iii).

Suppose finally that the pairing separates $P$. Then a $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module structure with a decomposition $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$ satisfying the three displayed conditions is the same data as a module structure with $M_\mu=\{v:K_hv=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}v\ \text{for all }h\in P^{\vee}\}$ for each $\mu$, together with $E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i}$ and $F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}$. Indeed, given the conditions one has, by step 2.1, $M_\mu\subseteq\{v:K_hv=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}v\ \forall h\}\subseteq M_{\mu}$ (the second inclusion because any vector of the direct sum with $K_hv=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}v$ for all $h$ has all its nontrivial label components in characters equal to $\chi_\mu$, hence in $M_\mu$ by separation); conversely the eigenspace equations for a decomposition into the $M_\mu$ directly give the scalar condition, and the containments are assumed. This is the usual type-one definition for a separating datum, and it completes the discussion of the definition.

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

Let $T$ and $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the free algebra and defining ideal of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], and put
$m_{ij}=1-a_{ij}$ and $\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij}$ for its displayed Serre
sums. Define $\omega,\psi,\tau:T\to T$ on generators by

$$\omega(E_i)=-F_i,\quad\omega(F_i)=-E_i,\quad\omega(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\psi(E_i)=E_i,\quad\psi(F_i)=F_i,\quad\psi(K_h)=K_{-h},$$

$$\tau(E_i)=F_i,\quad\tau(F_i)=E_i,\quad\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}.$$

Here $\omega$ fixes $\mathbb Q(q)$, while $\psi$ and $\tau$ apply the field
involution $q\mapsto q^{-1}$ to coefficients; $\omega$ and $\psi$ extend as
algebra maps, and $\tau$ extends as an anti-algebra map. Each map preserves

involutions; $\omega$ is a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra automorphism, $\psi$ a
semilinear algebra automorphism, and $\tau$ a semilinear algebra
anti-involution. On the Serre sums,

$$\omega(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij},\qquad\psi(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij},\qquad\tau(\mathrm{Serre}^{\pm}_{ij})=(-1)^{1-a_{ij}}\mathrm{Serre}^{\mp}_{ij}.$$

To check the common scalar, write $\sigma(E_i)=q_i^{-1}K_i^{-1}F_i$ and move all toral factors left. The crossing exponent is $-d_i m(m-1)-d_i ma_{ij}=0$, since $m=1-a_{ij}$; the negative case uses $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$ with the same exponent. Hence $\sigma$ descends to an anti-algebra endomorphism of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$; since $\sigma^2$ fixes every generator and is an algebra endomorphism ($\sigma^2(xy)=\sigma(\sigma(y)\sigma(x))=\sigma^2(x)\sigma^2(y)$), $\sigma^2=\mathrm{id}$, so $\sigma$ is an involutive anti-automorphism, $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, with $\sigma(K_h)=K_h$ and distinct from the semilinear $\tau$ of [F5].

If $B$ satisfies condition (iv), then for $x=K_h,E_i,F_i$ one gets the three displays by substituting $\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$, $\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$. Conversely, assume the three displays hold. Let $S\subseteq U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the set of $x$ with $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all $u,v\in M$. It contains $1$ (since $\sigma(1)=1$ and $B(u,v)=B(u,v)$) and the generators; if $x,y\in S$, then $B((xy)u,v)=B(x(yu),v)=B(yu,\sigma(x)v)=B(u,\sigma(y)\sigma(x)v)=B(u,\sigma(xy)v)$ by step 1.1, so $xy\in S$. Hence $S=U_q(\mathfrak g)$, which is condition (iv). In particular $\sigma$ fixes the torus, so $B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv)$: the form is toral-invariant and not toral-inverting.

Uniqueness holds even without assuming symmetry or homogeneity. For two normalized $\sigma$-contravariant bilinear forms put $D=B-B'$. For every nonempty negative word $w$, $\sigma(w)v_\lambda=0$, and contravariance applied to $\sigma(w)$ gives $D(v_\lambda,wv_\lambda)=D(\sigma(w)v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=0$; for the empty word this is normalization. Thus $B=B'$, and this uniqueness may be applied to a form and its transpose before symmetry is established.

Homogeneity and orthogonality of different characters: let $u\in M_\mu$, $v\in M_\tau$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$. By step 2.1, $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}B(u,v)=B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv)=q^{\langle\tau,h\rangle}B(u,v)$; since $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}\ne q^{\langle\tau,h\rangle}$ unless the characters agree, $B(u,v)=0$ whenever $\chi_\mu\ne\chi_\tau$. This is condition (ii), restated as a proved orthogonality: label-weight spaces with different characters are orthogonal, so under a separating pairing distinct label-weight spaces are orthogonal.

In the separating case, nondegeneracy of the global form passes to each finite-dimensional label-weight space: if the pairing separates $P$ and $b\in M_\mu$ satisfies $B(b,M_\mu)=0$, then $B(b,M_\tau)=0$ for every $\tau\ne\mu$ by step 3.1 and $B(b,M_\mu)=0$ by assumption, so $b$ lies in the radical of $B$ on $M$; hence $b=0$ whenever $B$ is nondegenerate on $M$. The remaining clauses are the content of the Cartan-projection lemma: for $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight module, `lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form` constructs the normalized homogeneous $\sigma$-invariant form on the Verma module $M(\lambda)$ (existence), identifies its radical with the maximal proper graded submodule, descends it to $L(\lambda)$ and proves nondegeneracy of the descended form. By step 2.2 that descended form is the unique one satisfying (i)-(iv). The existence and nondegeneracy clauses of this definition are thus delegated to that declared supplier, which is proved on this page; every other clause of the definition is proved above.

Step 1.1 defines sigma on generators and step 4.1 proves uniqueness directly by contravariance; no choices or height induction are required.

the same step 2.1 derives B(xu,v)=B(u,sigma(x)v) for arbitrary x from the three displays, and step 4.1 adds that in the separating case this yields nondegeneracy label by label.

Read Definition/Facts/Verification 1.1–4.1 against DJ relations, symmetrizer row convention, Chevalley maps, triangular decomposition, labels and dominance. The anti-map fixes q and K_h; moving toral factors through m=1-a_ij letters cancels the crossing exponent and gives (-1)^m q_i^-m q_j^-1 for both Serre images. Generator adjunctions extend by linearity and multiplication. A nonempty negative word is killed after applying sigma to the highest vector, giving uniqueness before transposition; distinct toral characters are orthogonal. Nondegeneracy on a weight space follows from global nondegeneracy and orthogonality, without identifying colliding labels. Existence and radical descent are explicitly deferred via justified_by to the level-2 Cartan-projection lemma, to be checked at its routed level. JKK (2.2)–(2.3), p.8, agrees with the linear convention. Normalization excludes a form on the zero module.

For a vector space $V$ over $k$, set $V^{\otimes0}=k$ and define the
**tensor algebra**

$$T(V)=\bigoplus_{n\geq0}V^{\otimes n}.$$

After fixing the canonical tensor-product associators, multiplication on
homogeneous pure tensors is concatenation:

$$ (v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_m)(w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n)=v_1\otimes\cdots\otimes v_m\otimes w_1\otimes\cdots\otimes w_n.$$

Extend this bilinearly. Each element has finite degree support, so products are
finite sums. Tensor associativity makes concatenation associative, and
$1\in k=V^{\otimes0}$ is its unit. Thus $T(V)$ is a graded unital associative
$k$-algebra. The degree-one inclusion is denoted $j:V\to T(V)$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

derivations.claim: Part (i): by [F1], $E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=E^{a+b}/([a]_i![b]_i!)=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{a+b}/[a+b]_i!=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)}$ and likewise for $F$.

Auxiliary product identity. Fix integers $a,b$ and $t\ge1$, put $c:=2t-a-b-2$ and let $G(x,t):=\prod_{s=1}^{t}(K_iq_i^{x-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{-x+s-1})$, so that $T_{i,x,t}=G(x,t)/D(t)$ with $D(t)=\prod_{s=1}^{t}(q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s})$; we prove $[a+1]_iT_{i,c+1,t}=[a-t+1]_iT_{i,c,t}+T_{i,t-b,1}T_{i,c,t-1}$. Factoring $G(x,t)=q_i^{-t(t-1)/2}\prod_{s=1}^{t}(K_iq_i^{x}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{2s-2-x})$ and putting $u:=K_iq_i^{c+1}$, so that $K_iq_i^{x}=uq_i^{x-c-1}$ and $K_i^{-1}q_i^{y}=u^{-1}q_i^{y+c+1}$, the relevant factors become $G(c+1,t)=q_i^{-t(t-1)/2}(u-u^{-1})W$, $G(c,t)=q_i^{-t(t-1)/2}q_i^{-t}W(u-q_i^{2t}u^{-1})$, $G(c,t-1)=q_i^{-(t-1)(t-2)/2}q_i^{-(t-1)}W$ and $G(t-b,1)=uq_i^{a-t+1}-u^{-1}q_i^{-a+t-1}$, where $W:=\prod_{s=1}^{t-1}(u-q_i^{2s}u^{-1})$. Multiplying the target identity by $D(t)=D(t-1)(q_i^{t}-q_i^{-t})$, using $D(t)/(D(t-1))=[t]_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ and $q_i^{t}-q_i^{-t}=[t]_i(q_i-q_i^{-1})$, and factoring out the common factor $q_i^{-t(t-1)/2}W$, the two sides become $[a+1]_i(u-u^{-1})$ and $[a-t+1]_iq_i^{-t}(u-q_i^{2t}u^{-1})+[t]_i(uq_i^{a-t+1}-u^{-1}q_i^{-a+t-1})$; comparing the coefficients of $u$ and $u^{-1}$ gives the identities $[a+1]_i=q_i^{-t}[a-t+1]_i+q_i^{a-t+1}[t]_i$ and $[a+1]_i=q_i^{t}[a-t+1]_i+q_i^{-a+t-1}[t]_i$, both instances of [F5] with $(m,n)=(a-t+1,t)$.

Part (ii): unrolling the product definition, $T_{i,c,t}=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{-c+s-1}}{q_i^{s}-q_i^{-s}}$ equals the $s=t$ factor times $T_{i,c,t-1}$; since both are Laurent polynomials in $K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], Verification) they commute and the recursion follows. The commutativity statements are those of that step. For the shifts, [F3] gives $E_jf(K_i^{\pm1})=f(q_i^{-a_{ij}}K_i^{\pm1})E_j$ and $F_jf(K_i^{\pm1})=f(q_i^{a_{ij}}K_i^{\pm1})F_j$; applying this to the $t$-fold product $f=T_{i,c,t}$, the first factor of $T_{i,c,t}$ is multiplied by $q_i^{-a_{ij}}$ (first term) and $q_i^{a_{ij}}$ (second term), which is the same as replacing $c$ by $c-a_{ij}$; hence $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$ (for $j=i$, $a_{ii}=2$), and likewise $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$. Rewriting gives $T_{i,c,t}E_j=E_jT_{i,c+a_{ij},t}$ and $T_{i,c,t}F_j=F_jT_{i,c-a_{ij},t}$.

Reordering by induction on $a$ for fixed $b$. At $a=0$ the identity is $F_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}T_{i,-b,0}E_i^{(0)}$. Multiply the formula for $a$ on the left by $E_i/[a+1]_i$. For a target index $1\le t\le\min(a+1,b)$ put $c=2t-a-b-2$. The no-contraction term from index $t$ contributes $[a-t+1]_iT_{i,c,t}$ to the coefficient of $F_i^{(b-t)}E_i^{(a+1-t)}$, after shifting $E_i$ through the toral factor. The contraction term from index $t-1$ contributes $T_{i,t-b,1}T_{i,c,t-1}$ by [F4]. Their sum is $[a+1]_iT_{i,c+1,t}$ by step 1.2, so division by the nonzero $[a+1]_i$ gives the target coefficient. When $t=a+1$ the absent no-contraction term is represented by $[0]_i=0$; the $t=0$ term is just $F_i^{(b)}E_i^{(a+1)}$. A contraction from $t=b$ is absent because $F_i^{(0)}=1$, so no target exceeds $b$. These account for every term and prove the induction, including the stated special cases.

The remaining clauses of (iii): for $i\ne j$ the relation $E_iF_j=F_jE_i$ of [F2] gives $E_i^{(a)}F_j^{(b)}=F_j^{(b)}E_i^{(a)}$ after dividing by the nonzero factorials [F1]; if $a_{ij}=0$ then $E_iE_j=E_jE_i$ and $F_iF_j=F_jF_i$ by [F2], hence $E_i^{(a)}E_j^{(b)}=E_j^{(b)}E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_i^{(a)}F_j^{(b)}=F_j^{(b)}F_i^{(a)}$ for all $a,b$. No commutation is asserted when $a_{ij}\ne0$, where the quantum Serre relation is the only comparison used later.

Part (iv): every element of $U_A$ is a finite $A$-linear combination of finite products of generators by [F6]. Move every $K_h^{\pm1}$ and every $T_{j,c,t}$ to the middle: $K_h$ commutes with the toral generators and crosses $E_j,F_j$ at the cost of the scalar $q^{\mp\langle\alpha_j,h\rangle}\in A$ by [F3]; $T_{j,c,t}$ crosses $E_i,F_i$ at the cost of an index shift by step 2.1. These operations do not change the relative order of the positive and negative generators, so after finitely many of them we obtain a finite sum of terms $b_-u\,b_+$ with $u\in U_A^0$ and $b_\pm$ products of divided powers of a single sign, except that a product may still contain an $E$-factor to the left of an $F$-factor. Define the measure of such a product as the pair (total height $h$ = sum of the exponents of all its divided powers, number $\iota$ of ordered pairs (positive factor, negative factor) in which the positive factor precedes the negative one), ordered lexicographically. An adjacent sign inversion, after moving toral factors aside, has the form $E_i^{(a)}F_j^{(b)}$ with $a,b\ge1$. If $i\ne j$, step 3.2 swaps the factors, keeping $h$ and decreasing $\iota$. If $i=j$, step 3.1 rewrites it as $\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}T_{i,2t-a-b,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$: the terms with $t\ge1$ strictly decrease $h$, while the $t=0$ term $F_i^{(b)}T_{i,-a-b,0}E_i^{(a)}$ keeps $h$ but strictly decreases $\iota$ (that inversion disappears and no other inversion is created, as toral factors are ignored by $\iota$). By induction on $(h,\iota)$ the rewriting terminates, producing the asserted span by triangular products in $U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$.

step 3.2 disposes of the degenerate index cases i!=j and a_ij=0, where no toral crossing factor appears, and the auxiliary identity of step 1.2 is proved for all integers a,b including negative ones.
Step 3.1 handles t=0, t=a+1 (the absent term represented by [0]=0), and t=b, giving the range 0 through min(a,b) in the Statement. Step 4.1 decreases height or inversions.

the lemma states identities rather than equivalences; both sides of the reordering identity are equalities derived from the same recursion, with no implication structure.
no converse is claimed: the spanning assertion of (iv) is one-directional, every element admitting a normal form, and it is proved by terminating rewriting in step 4.1.

[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of

write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.
