citations.quote:
Let $K$ be a field and let $v$ be a discrete valuation on $K$
([[def-discrete-valuation]]). Its **valuation ring** is
$$ V_v:=\{x\in K:v(x)\ge 0\}. $$
This is a valuation ring in the sense of [[def-valuation-ring]].

A **discrete valuation ring** (DVR) is a subring $V\subseteq K$ of the form
$V=V_v$ for some discrete valuation $v$ on $K$. Because $v$ is surjective,
there is an element of value $1$, so $V$ has a nonunit and is therefore not a
field.
Every finitely generated torsion-free module over a principal ideal domain is finite free.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]] with its root-lattice grading $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$. Define

$$U_q^+:=\langle E_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^-:=\langle F_i\ :\ i\in I\rangle,\qquad U_q^0:=\langle K_h\ :\ h\in P^{\vee}\rangle,$$

the $\mathbb Q(q)$-subalgebras generated by the indicated images, and let $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Then

$$U_q^\pm=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q_+}U_q^\pm[\pm\beta],\qquad U_q^+[\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cap U_q^+,\quad U_q^-[ -\beta]:=U_q(\mathfrak g)[-\beta]\cap U_q^-.$$

The degree-zero component $U_q(\mathfrak g)[0]$ contains $U_q^0$, and for every $x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ and $h\in P^{\vee}$,

$$K_hxK_h^{-1}=q^{\beta(h)}x.$$

Thus each $K_h\in U_q^0$ acts by conjugation on the degree-$\beta$ component as the scalar $q^{\beta(h)}$. The elements $K_h$ span $U_q^0$ and satisfy $K_hK_{h'}=K_{h+h'}$ with $K_0=1$; hence $U_q^0$ is a quotient of the group algebra $\mathbb Q(q)[P^{\vee}]$. The subalgebras $U_q^\pm$ are spanned by finite monomials in the $E_i$ and $F_i$, respectively. Define the nonnegative and nonpositive product spans by

$$U_q^{\ge0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^0U_q^+),\qquad U_q^{\le0}:=\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb Q(q)}(U_q^-U_q^0).$$

This definition asserts no linear independence of these spanning families and no injectivity of the natural maps; those claims belong to [[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]].

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

For a finite symmetrizable GCM over $\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak r^\pm$ is the ideal of the free half $\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^\pm$ generated by $(\operatorname{ad}e_i)^{1-a_{ij}}e_j$ or $(\operatorname{ad}f_i)^{1-a_{ij}}f_j$, respectively, for $i\ne j$. Hence $\mathfrak g(A)$ has exactly the Cartan relations and both Serre families as a presentation. Its halves have the corresponding separate Serre presentations, and multiplication gives the vector-space isomorphism $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak h)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)\cong U(\mathfrak g)$.

Let $L$ be a complex Lie algebra with a supplied finite or countable ordered basis $(x_i)$. The products $x_{i_1}\cdots x_{i_m}$ with $i_1\le\cdots\le i_m$, including $1$ for $m=0$, form a basis of $U(L)$. Consequently $L\to U(L)$ is injective. For the finite-word graded algebras here, compatible homogeneous bases of subalgebras and quotients can be obtained without AC.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), put
$A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ ([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), let
$L:=\sum_{i\in I}\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)\subseteq P^{\vee}$, and let $U_A^0$ be the
$A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the toral quantum
binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]).

(a) **One simple torus.** Fix $i\in I$ and write $z:=q_i$, $K:=K_i$,
$T_t:=T_{i,0,t}$ for $t\ge0$. Then for all $r,s\ge0$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and
$t\ge1$,
$$T_rT_s=\sum_{j=0}^{\min(r,s)}z^{rs}K^{-j}\binom{r+s-j}{r}_z\binom{r}{j}_zT_{r+s-j},\qquad T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^{-1}z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1},$$
where $\binom{m}{r}_z$ is the Gaussian binomial of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]; all
coefficients lie in $A$. Moreover the $A$-subalgebra of $U_q^0$ generated by
$K^{\pm1}$ and all $T_{c,t}$ equals the $A$-span of
$\{K^{\delta}T_t:\delta\in\{0,1\},\,t\ge0\}$, and that set is an $A$-basis.

(b) **Full torus.** Fix a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $P^{\vee}$, let $J$ be the
finite set of coordinates occurring in the finitely many vectors $d_ih_i$, and
let $D:=\bigoplus_{j\in J}\mathbb Z e_j$ be the corresponding coordinate direct
summand. For every coset of $L$ in $P^{\vee}$ choose the representative $c$
whose $D$-component has minimal sum of coordinate absolute values, ties broken
lexicographically, and whose complementary component is the coset's common
complementary component. Then
$$U_A^0=\bigoplus_{c}K_c\cdot A\text{-span}\Bigl\{\prod_{i\in I}K_i^{\delta_i}T_{i,0,t_i}:\delta_i\in\{0,1\},\,t_i\ge0\Bigr\},$$
the sum over the chosen representatives, so the displayed elements form an
$A$-basis of $U_A^0$.

Both statements are proved directly on the unmodified generators over the
non-PID ring $A$: no integral PBW or canonical-basis input, no inference from
torsion-freeness to freeness, and no modified-${}_A\dot U$ result is used.

A **free abelian group on a set $X$** is an abelian group $A(X)$ together with
a map $i:X\to A(X)$ such that, for every abelian group $B$ and every
function $u:X\to B$, there is a unique group homomorphism
$\widehat u:A(X)\to B$ satisfying

$$\widehat u\circ i=u.$$

derivations.claim: The localized form. The map $A\to R$ inverts exactly the elements of $A$ with nonzero value at $1$: it inverts all nonzero integers, while keeping $q-1$ noninvertible. For an $A$-submodule $N$ of a $\mathbb Q(q)$-space, its localization is its $R$-span in that space: every tensor is a common-denominator fraction $n/s$, and its image vanishes only if $n=0$. This identifies $U_A\otimes_A R$ and its three factors with their generated $R$-subalgebras. The valuation description in [F1] supplies the local PID properties.

The halves are finite free and specialize to the classical halves. Fix a root $
u$. By [F2] and [F1], $E_i^{(r)}=E_i^r/[r]_i!$ and $F_i^{(r)}=F_i^r/[r]_i!$ with $[r]_i!\in R^{	imes}$, so $U_R^+[
u]$ is generated as an $R$-module by the ordinary words $E_{i_1}\cdots E_{i_k}$ of degree $
u$ (finitely many for fixed $
u$); it is torsion-free inside the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space $U_q^+[
u]$, hence finitely generated torsion-free, hence free over the PID $R$ by [F1], of rank $\dim_{\mathbb Q(q)}U_q^+[
u]$; the same holds on the negative side. The $q=1$ fibre is generated by the same words, and the quantum Serre relations of the free algebra specialize coefficientwise to the classical Serre relations, so there is a surjection from the classical half $U(\mathfrak n^+)[
u]$ onto the fibre $U_R^+[
u]\otimes_RR/(q-1)$; both are finite-dimensional over the residue field $\mathbb Q$, with dimensions equal to the generic dimension by [F3]'s rank comparison (the only AC use, inherited here). A surjection of finite-dimensional spaces of equal dimension is an isomorphism, so the fibre is $U(\mathfrak n^+)_{\mathbb Q}[
u]$, and likewise for $U^-$. This proves (a).

The toral basis through $H_i$. Fix one node and put $z=q_i$, $K=K_i$, $H=T_{i,0,1}$ and $a=z-z^{-1}$. Then $K^{-1}=K-aH$ and $K^2=1+aKH$. For each integer $b$ use the extension $[b]_i:=(z^b-z^{-b})/(z-z^{-1})$ of the nonnegative quantum-integer convention. For $s\ge1$ the exact factor identity is $(Kz^b-K^{-1}z^{-b})/(z^s-z^{-s})=([b]_iK+z^{-b}H)/[s]_i$. Since $[s]_i\in R^\times$, all toral binomials lie in $R[K^{\pm1},H]$. The two relations for $K$ show this algebra is spanned by $\{K^\delta H^t:\delta=0,1,\ t\ge0\}$: it is closed under $K$, $K^{-1}$ and $H$. In a finite linear relation among these elements, take the largest $t=N$. The nonzero coefficient of $K^{N+1}$ in $KH^N$ isolates its coefficient; after removing it, the nonzero coefficient of $K^{-N}$ in $H^N$ isolates its coefficient. Descending proves independence over $\mathbb Q(q)$, hence over $R$. For the finitely many independent nodes, tensor these bases and multiply by the representatives $K_c$ of $P^\vee/L$; the direct group-algebra coset decomposition in [F7] proves independence and spanning, giving (b)'s toral basis.

Triangular decomposition over $R$. Each half component is free by step 1.2 and the torus is free by step 1.3, so their tensor product is free and embeds into its fraction-field extension. The field-level multiplication of [F5] is injective there, hence its restriction is injective. Surjectivity follows from the integral triangular spanning proved in [[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]](iv), after localization; containing algebra generators alone would not suffice for a linear image. Thus multiplication $U_R^-\otimes_RU_R^0\otimes_RU_R^+\to U_R$ is an isomorphism.

The toral specialization and its positive quotient. The toral algebra has the presentation $R[P^\vee][H_i:i\in I]/(K_i-K_i^{-1}-(q_i-q_i^{-1})H_i:i\in I)$. Indeed it maps onto $U_R^0$ by step 1.3. In each simple-node factor, $K_i^2-(q_i-q_i^{-1})K_iH_i-1$ is monic in $K_i$ and gives $K_i^{-1}=K_i-(q_i-q_i^{-1})H_i$, so the presented algebra has basis $K_i^\delta H_i^t$. The group algebra $R[P^\vee]$ is free over $R[L]$ on the coset representatives; extending the finitely many node presentations therefore gives exactly the basis of step 1.3, proving injectivity. Every characteristic-zero specialization $A\to k$, $q\mapsto1$, factors through $R$. Reduction gives $U_A^0\otimes_A k\cong k[P^\vee/2L]\otimes_k k[H_i]$. Quotienting by all $K_h-1$ is the group-algebra augmentation in the first factor and yields $k[H_i]$ with exactly that kernel. With $b=c-s+1$, the factor identity in step 1.3 reduces in this quotient to $(H_i+b)/s$, hence $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\prod_{s=1}^t(H_i+c-s+1)/s=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$.

The full positive quotient. In $U_A\otimes_A k$, every $K_h$ commutes with the halves because its crossing scalars $q^{\langle\alpha_j,h\rangle}$ specialize to $1$. Consequently the ideal generated by $K_h-1$ is, under the tensor decomposition of step 2.1, exactly $U(\mathfrak n^-)_k\otimes (K_h-1)_h(U_A^0\otimes_A k)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)_k$. The quotient thus has tensor space $U(\mathfrak n^-)_k\otimes k[H_i]\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)_k$. The mixed relation specializes to $[e_i,f_j]=\delta_{ij}H_i$; the toral shifts give $[H_i,e_j]=a_{ij}e_j$ and $[H_i,f_j]=-a_{ij}f_j$, using step 2.2; and both Serre families specialize to the classical relations. The presentation in [F4] gives a surjection $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k\to Q$. It is an isomorphism on the three factors of the classical PBW tensor decomposition: on the halves by step 1.2, and on the torus by step 2.2. Multiplication intertwines these decompositions, so the full map is injective as well. The rational classical presentations used here have the same ranks as their complex extensions: in each finite word component, extension from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb C$ preserves linear independence and kernels; [F4]'s complex Serre and PBW results therefore descend to $\mathbb Q$ and extend to any characteristic-zero $k$. This proves (c).

Boundaries. For the standard rank-one torus, the generic character $E=F=0$, $K=-1$ respects the quantum relations and restricts to an $A$-valued character of $U_A$: $T_{c,t}$ maps to $(-1)^t\prod_{s=1}^t[c-s+1]_i/[s]_i$, denoted $(-1)^t\binom{c}{t}_i$ with this product convention for integer $c$. For $c=-b<0$, each numerator $[-b-s+1]_i=-[b+s-1]_i$ contributes a second sign, so the character value is $\binom{b+t-1}{t}_i$, a Laurent polynomial; for $c\ge0$ Laurent integrality is supplied by [[lem-quantum-pascal-recurrence-and-gaussian-integrality]]. The specialized character has $K=-1$, so the unquotiented specialization retains this character. All local divisions above are by units $[r]_i!$ or $[s]_i$; the factors $q_i-q_i^{-1}$ have valuation one and were canceled in the exact rational identity of step 1.3 before reduction. No vanishing denominator is inverted in $R$ or separately substituted at $q=1$.

boundaries.evidence: the halves are indexed by roots nu; the zero root component U_R^pm[0] is R*1, and step 1.2's word-generation statement for nu=0 is generated by the empty word, while step 1.3 covers t=0 with H^0=1.

the fibre at q=1 is taken by base change, not by substituting zero; step 1.1 notes A->R is a localization hence flat, and step 2.2 shows the quotient by all K_h-1 leaves the polynomial algebra rather than the zero ring.
Step 1.1 keeps q-1 noninvertible. Step 1.3 divides only by [s]_i, whose value at 1 is nonzero, and step 2.2 then imposes K_h=1 by the group-algebra augmentation.

step 4.1 exhibits the degenerate unquotiented specialization with E=F=0 and K=-1 for sl2, showing that K_h=1 cannot be asserted before quotienting; extra Cartan directions are discussed through the positive quotient of step 3.1.
Step 1.2 matches the generic and classical half dimensions in each root degree. Step 2.1 uses the product factors to obtain T(c,0)=1 and T(c,1)=H_i+c in the positive quotient.

boundaries.reason: AC enters only through the generic rank theorem [F3](i); the localizations, the toral basis of step 1.3 and the fibre comparisons of step 1.2 are explicit and choice-free.
the theorem asserts isomorphisms and quotient identifications, not a biconditional; the halves, the torus, the triangular decomposition and the positive quotient are four separate claims.
no converse is claimed: step 4.1 is explicitly an honest boundary recording what is NOT asserted about the unquotiented specialization rather than a reverse implication.

Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, over $k=\mathbb Q(q)$, and let $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ be its generated subalgebras of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]].

(i) Multiplication is a vector-space isomorphism
$$m:U_q^-\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+\longrightarrow U_q(\mathfrak g),\qquad x_-\otimes x_0\otimes x_+\longmapsto x_-x_0x_+.$$
Products $b_-K_h b_+$, with $b_\pm$ ranging over supplied bases of the two halves and $h\in P^\vee$, form a basis of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$. Arbitrary simple-generator words span the halves; their Serre relations preclude claiming their independence.

(ii) The halves are exactly the algebras presented by their separate Serre relations, and $U_q^0\cong k[P^\vee]$. Thus all three abstract factor maps are injective and the $K_h$ are linearly independent.

(iii) For every $\beta\in Q$, the total root grading satisfies
$$U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]\cong\bigoplus_{\alpha,\gamma\in Q_+,\,\alpha-\gamma=\beta} U_q^-[-\gamma]\otimes_k U_q^0\otimes_k U_q^+[\alpha].$$
In particular degree zero contains all equal-positive/negative-degree summands, including $F_iE_i$; it is not just the toral subalgebra. As a left $U_q^0$-module this component is free, with rank equal to the possibly infinite sum of the products of the two half-component dimensions. Under AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), the half-component dimensions are their classical PBW ranks, and products of the generic PBW bases of [[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]] with the toral basis give a PBW basis of the whole algebra. AC enters only through that supplier's formal-embedding proof; (i), (ii) and the graded tensor decomposition are choice-free.

A **symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group** consists of a finite nonempty index set $I=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a symmetrizable generalized Cartan matrix $A=(a_{ij})_{i,j\in I}$ ([[def-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[def-symmetrizable-generalized-cartan-matrix]]) and a chosen diagonal symmetrizer $D=\operatorname{diag}(d_1,\ldots,d_n)$ with $d_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}$ and $d_i a_{ij}=d_j a_{ji}$ for all $i,j$; free abelian groups $P^\vee$ and $P$ ([[def-free-abelian-group]]) with an integer-valued bilinear pairing $\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^\vee\to\mathbb Z$; simple coroots $h_i\in P^\vee$ that are linearly independent in $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$; and simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ that freely generate the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i\subseteq P$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]) and satisfy $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ for all $i,j$ ([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]], [[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

The index set is finite and $A$ need not be nonsingular. We do not require the simple coroots to span $P^\vee\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$, and the pairing is not required to be perfect; choosing $P$ and $P^\vee$ is part of the datum, not something determined by the matrix alone.

We fix an indeterminate $q$ over $\mathbb Q$, work over $\mathbb Q(q)$, and set $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $h\in P^\vee$, $\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ is the exponent in $q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}$. We use the row convention $\langle\alpha_j,h_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ throughout. No fundamental weights with prescribed values on all $h_i$ are part of this definition.

Let $U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ be the negative half of the
Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with its skew derivations $e_i'$
([[def-kashiwara-skew-derivations-on-the-negative-quantum-half]],
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]), and let
$\varepsilon\colon U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ be the **augmentation**, the projection
onto the degree-zero component $U_q^-[0]=\mathbb Q(q)\cdot1$ (so
$\varepsilon(Q)=0$ on all positive-height components and $\varepsilon(1)=1$).

The **normalized Lusztig–Kashiwara form** on $U_q^-$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon U_q^-\times U_q^-\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(H) $B$ is **homogeneous**: $B\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu],U_q^-[-\mu]\bigr)=0$ whenever
$\nu\ne\mu$;

(N) $B(1,1)=1$;

(R) $B(F_iP,Q)=B(P,e_i'Q)$ for all $i\in I$ and all $P,Q\in U_q^-$.

Equivalently, axioms (H) and (N) may be replaced by the single **counit
normalization**

(C) $B(1,Q)=\varepsilon(Q)$ for all $Q\in U_q^-$,

in the presence of (R) (Verification, step 1.1).

Axioms (H) and (N) (equivalently (C)) are essential and not redundant: the
recursion (R) together with $B(1,1)=1$ alone neither forces symmetry nor
uniqueness, as the rank-one witness of step 2.2 shows.

The axioms determine $B$ uniquely: peeling first letters in the first argument
writes every positive-height $P$ as a finite sum $P=\sum_iF_iP_i$ and evaluates
$B(P,Q)=\sum_iB(P_i,e_i'Q)$, reducing the height; the base of the induction is
(C) (Verification, step 2.1). The **existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy** of
$B$ on $U_q^-$ for the actual quotient by the Serre ideal are not proved here:
they are the content of the negative-half form theorem
`thm-the-negative-half-bilinear-form-is-symmetric-nondegenerate-and-integral`,
the declared justification of this definition, which also settles the exact
integrality normalization ($A$-valuedness on the word lattice and the
Gaussian-factorial denominators on the divided-power lattice). That theorem
is proved on this page, and its statement is the declared supplier of
existence, symmetry and nondegeneracy; this definition itself claims only that
(H), (N) and (R) determine $B$ and that the normalization cannot be relaxed.

Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra of
[[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], with its generated
subalgebras $U_q^-,U_q^0,U_q^+$ and root gradings
$U_q^-=\bigoplus_{\nu\in Q_+}U_q^-[-\nu]$ of
[[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]
($Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$, height $\operatorname{ht}$ of
[[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]). Fix $i\in I$ and
write $K_i:=K_{d_ih_i}$, so that $K_iF_jK_i^{-1}=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j$ and
$q_i-q_i^{-1}\ne0$.

For every $P\in U_q^-$ there exist unique elements $Q,R\in U_q^-$ with

$$E_iP-PE_i=\frac{K_iQ-K_i^{-1}R}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}.$$

Define the **Kashiwara skew derivations** $e_i',e_i'':U_q^-\to U_q^-$ by

$$e_i'(P):=R\qquad\text{and}\qquad e_i''(P):=Q .$$

Thus $e_i'$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i^{-1}$ and
$e_i''$ is the operator whose value is the coefficient of $K_i$ in the
commutator with $E_i$. The maps have the following properties, all proved in
the Verification below.

(a) $e_i'$ and $e_i''$ are $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, vanish on $1$, and
$e_i'(F_j)=e_i''(F_j)=\delta_{ij}$ for all $j\in I$.

(b) (Twisted Leibniz rules) For homogeneous $x,y\in U_q^-$, with the actual
weight $\operatorname{wt}(x)\in Q$ of [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]],
$$e_i'(xy)=e_i'(x)y+q_i^{\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i'(y),\qquad e_i''(xy)=e_i''(x)y+q_i^{-\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}x\,e_i''(y).$$

(c) (Commutation with the generators) For all $j\in I$ and all $y\in U_q^-$,
$$e_i'(F_jy)=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i'(y)+\delta_{ij}y,\qquad e_i''(F_jy)=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_j\,e_i''(y)+\delta_{ij}y,$$

equivalently $e_i'F_j=q_i^{-a_{ij}}F_je_i'+\delta_{ij}$ and
$e_i''F_j=q_i^{a_{ij}}F_je_i''+\delta_{ij}$ as operators on $U_q^-$.

(d) (Grading, height and nilpotence) For every $\nu\in Q_+$,

$$e_i'\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr),\ e_i''\bigl(U_q^-[-\nu]\bigr)\ \subseteq\ U_q^-[ -(\nu-\alpha_i)],$$

the right-hand side being $0$ when $\nu-\alpha_i\notin Q_+$. In particular both
maps raise the actual weight by $\alpha_i$, lower the positive height by one,
and are locally nilpotent: $(e_i')^{k}(P)=(e_i'')^{k}(P)=0$ for $k$ larger than
the height of the degree of a homogeneous $P$.

(e) (Bar compatibility) Let $\psi$ be the semilinear algebra involution
$q\mapsto q^{-1}$, $E_i\mapsto E_i$, $F_i\mapsto F_i$, $K_h\mapsto K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].
Then $e_i''=\psi\,e_i'\,\psi$ on $U_q^-$.

The commutator construction also fixes the orientation: the
$K_i^{-1}$-coefficient is $e_i'$ and the $K_i$-coefficient is $e_i''$. The
twists $q_i^{\pm\langle\operatorname{wt}(x),h_i\rangle}$ in (b) are the twists
of the corresponding coefficient maps of the negative-half coproduct in the
source's dictionary; the explicit commutator computation used here is the
definition of record, and no imaginary-simple-root convention is needed, since
every Cartan datum of this library has $a_{ii}=2$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $\mathbb Z[t]$ be the polynomial ring over the integers
([[def-polynomial-ring-over-a-commutative-ring]],
[[thm-polynomial-ring-is-a-commutative-ring]]) and let
$$S=\{t^k:k\ge0\}.$$
The set $S$ is multiplicative, and the **Laurent polynomial ring** is the
principal localisation
$$\Lambda_1:=\mathbb Z[t]_S=S^{-1}\mathbb Z[t]$$
([[def-principal-localisation]], [[def-multiplicative-subset-and-localisation]]).
It is a commutative ring with unit $1=t^0$ ([[def-commutative-ring]]). Write
again $t$ for the image of the indeterminate under the localisation map; then
$t$ is a unit with inverse $t^{-1}$
([[prop-units-in-a-localisation]]). Every element of $\Lambda_1$ has a
representative
$$\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k,\qquad a_k\in\mathbb Z,$$
with only finitely many nonzero coefficients, obtained by writing a fraction
$p/t^N$ as a finite $\mathbb Z$-linear combination of the powers
$t^{k-N}$; the finite coefficient sequence is unique: after multiplying two such sums
by a common sufficiently large power of $t$, equality becomes equality of
ordinary polynomials. The localisation map $\mathbb Z[t]\to\Lambda_1$ is
injective because $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain; hence their coefficients agree
([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]]). Equivalently, two such
sums are equal exactly when their coefficient sequences agree
([[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]).

**Universal property.** Let $A$ be a ring with unit and let
$\varphi\colon\mathbb Z[t]\to A$ be a unital ring homomorphism with
$\varphi(t)$ a unit of $A$. Then there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\widetilde\varphi\colon\Lambda_1\to A$ with
$\widetilde\varphi(t)=\varphi(t)$. Equivalently, for every unital ring $A$ and
every unit $u\in A$ there is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$\Lambda_1\to A$ with $t\mapsto u$ ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]],
[[def-ring-homomorphism]]).

The cited localisation theorem treats commutative target rings. For the
possibly noncommutative target used here, define
$\sum_k a_kt^k\mapsto\sum_k(a_k1_A)u^k$. Unique Laurent coefficients make
this well defined. Integer multiples of $1_A$ are central, and
$u^ku^l=u^{k+l}$ for all integers $k,l$, so finite distributivity proves
additivity, multiplicativity and preservation of $1$. Every unital
homomorphism must send $a_k$ to $a_k1_A$ and $t^k$ to $u^k$, proving
uniqueness. Taking $u=\varphi(t)$ gives the asserted extension of $\varphi$.

**Augmentation.** There is a unique unital ring homomorphism
$$\varepsilon\colon\Lambda_1\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad \varepsilon\Bigl(\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k\Bigr)=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k,$$
the **sum-of-coefficients map** ([[thm-universal-property-of-localisation]]); it
is well defined because the coefficients are summable and their total sum is
unchanged along the relation of
[[prop-localisation-zero-equality-and-kernel-criteria]]. Its kernel is the
principal ideal $(t-1)$: indeed $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$, and if
$\varepsilon(x)=0$ then, writing $x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_kt^k$ with finite
support and using that $\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k=0$, one has
$$x=\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k(t^k-1)=(t-1)\sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}a_k\,(1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}),$$
where $1+t+\cdots+t^{k-1}$ denotes the empty sum $0$ for $k=0$ and, for
$k=-j<0$, the negative sum
$-(t^{-1}+t^{-2}+\cdots+t^{-j})$, so that
$t^{-j}-1=-(t-1)(t^{-1}+\cdots+t^{-j})$; hence $x\in(t-1)$, and the reverse
inclusion is $\varepsilon(t-1)=0$.

**Caveats.** This item realises $\Lambda_1$ by localisation and does **not**
identify it with an integral group ring: the additive group underlying
$\Lambda_1$ is $\bigoplus_{k\in\mathbb Z}\mathbb Z\,t^k$ and its multiplication
is the polynomial one ([[cor-polynomial-ring-over-a-domain-is-a-domain]] is not
needed for the ring laws but records that $\mathbb Z[t]$ is a domain). The
deck-module structures on homology introduced later on this page are defined
separately, by the universal property above.

Adjunction, symmetry and uniqueness. In the braided coproduct of a word $w=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$, the component with first factor of degree $-\alpha_i$ is $\sum_{t:j_t=i}q^{-\sum_{s<t}\langle\alpha_{j_s},\alpha_i\rangle}f_i\otimes\varphi_-(w\setminus t)$: the letter at position $t$ crosses precisely the earlier letters assigned to the second factor. The rescaled Hopf adjunction of step 1.1 therefore gives $B(F_iP,w)=\sum_{t:j_t=i}q_i^{-\sum_{s<t}a_{ij_s}}B(P,w\setminus t)=B(P,e_i'w)$ by [F3]; unequal degrees give zero on both sides, so this proves (R) for all $P,Q$ by linearity. Repeated deletion gives, for equal-length words $u=F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_m}$ and $v=F_{j_1}\cdots F_{j_m}$, the formula $B(u,v)=\sum_\pi q^{-\sum_{a<b,\,\pi(a)>\pi(b)}\langle\alpha_{i_a},\alpha_{i_b}\rangle}$, where $\pi$ ranges over bijections with $j_{\pi(a)}=i_a$; if their color degrees differ the value is zero. Indeed the first deletion chooses $\pi(1)$, its crossing exponent records exactly the inversions involving that first letter, and induction accounts for the remaining inversions, with empty-word value $1$. The map $\pi\mapsto\pi^{-1}$ preserves the exponent after interchanging the two words because the color form is symmetric, so $B$ is symmetric. Finally [F2] identifies every normalized homogeneous form satisfying (R) with $B$. This proves (i), without attributing existence or symmetry to the Statement of the separation lemma.

Integrality on the word lattice. We show $B(u,v)\in A$ for classes of words $u,v$ by induction on the total height of $u$ plus $\deg v$ (in fact on the height of the first argument): if $u=1$, then $B(1,v)=\varepsilon(v)\in\{0,1\}\subseteq A$; if $u=F_iw$ then $B(u,v)=B(w,e_i'v)$, and $e_i'v$ is an $A$-linear combination of classes of words of strictly smaller height by [F3], so the induction hypothesis applies. By bilinearity $B(W,W)\subseteq A$, and $W\subseteq U_A^-$ because $F_i^k=[k]_i!F_i^{(k)}$ with $[k]_i!\in A$ by [F4].

The rank-one divided-power values. Fix $i$ and assume $I=\{i\}$ for the computation, so that the rank-one subalgebra is the free algebra on $F_i$ and $e_i'(F_i^m)=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_iF_i^{m-1}$ by inducting on $m$ from $e_i'F_i^m=q_i^{-2}F_ie_i'F_i^{m-1}+F_i^{m-1}$. Dividing by $[m]_i!$ gives $e_i'(F_i^{(m)})=q_i^{-(m-1)}F_i^{(m-1)}$. Put $b_m:=B(F_i^{(m)},F_i^{(m)})$. Using $F_i^{(m)}=[m]_i^{-1}F_iF_i^{(m-1)}$ and (R), $b_m=[m]_i^{-1}B(F_i^{(m-1)},e_i'(F_i^{(m)}))=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_i^{-1}b_{m-1}$ with $b_0=1$, so $b_m=q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}/[m]_i!$. By [F4], $[m]_i!=q_i^{-m(m-1)/2}[m]_{q_i^2}!$, hence $b_m=1/[m]_{q_i^2}!=\prod_{j=1}^m(1+\cdots+q_i^{2(j-1)})^{-1}$; for $m\ne n$ the two divided powers have different heights, so $B(F_i^{(m)},F_i^{(n)})=0$ by homogeneity. At $m=2$ this is $1/(1+q_i^2)\notin A$ by [F5]. This proves the rank-one clause of (iv) and shows that the form is not $A$-valued on $U_A^-$.

The right-adjunction failure and the global denominator bound. First, no constant $c$ makes $(P,QF_i)=c(e_i''P,Q)$ hold on the rank-one subalgebra: $(F_i,F_i)=B(F_i,F_i)=1$ and $(F_i,F_i\cdot1)=1$ force $c=1$ from $(e_i''F_i,1)=(1,1)=1$, but $(F_i^2,F_i^2)=[2]_i^2b_2=(q_i+q_i^{-1})^2/(1+q_i^2)=1+q_i^{-2}$ while $(e_i''F_i^2,F_i)=(1+q_i^2)(F_i,F_i)=1+q_i^2$, which differs; this justifies the parenthetical in (i). Second, every element of $U_A^-$ is an $A$-linear combination of divided-power words $\prod_iF_i^{(r_i)}$ with coefficients in $A$ (the divided powers generate $U_A^-$ by definition), and each such word is its underlying ordinary word divided by the finite product $\prod_i[r_i]_i!$; by bilinearity of $B$ and $B(W,W)\subseteq A$ from step 3.1, $B(U_A^-,U_A^-)\subseteq A_{\mathrm{loc}}=A[s^{-1}:s\in S]$. Since $[r]_i!=q_i^{-r(r-1)/2}[r]_{q_i^2}!$ by [F4] and $q_i^{\pm1}\in A^{\times}$, inverting the $[r]_i!$ is the same as inverting the Gaussian factorials $[r]_{q_i^2}!$; the bound is exact in rank one by step 3.2. This completes (iv).

risk_review.notes: Accepted the corrected multiplicative set generated by all quantum factorials. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 and every ten dependency interfaces, with the previously reviewed separation proof supplying the constructed homogeneous symmetric nondegenerate form, not merely its headline separation assertion. Peeling from the augmentation row proves uniqueness; component orthogonality plus finite support gives global nondegeneracy in both directions. Deletion on words has Laurent coefficients, proving A-valuedness on the word lattice. Rank-one divided norms satisfy b_m=q_i^-(m-1)b_(m-1)/[m]_i, so b_2=1/(1+q_i^2) is outside A (augmentation would require an integer reciprocal of 2). Any divided-power word has factorial-product denominators, giving the stated localization bound; S must contain finite products, as now stated. A constant right-adjunction against e_i'' fails at degree two after degree one forces c=1. The empty word and m=0,1 match normalization. AC is inherited only from the separation/generic-pairing supplier. This discharges the level-1 half-form definition's existence/symmetry/nondegeneracy obligation; no A-integrality on the larger divided lattice is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), $A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$
([[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]), and
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$, so that $R$ is a DVR with
uniformizer $q-1$ ([[def-discrete-valuation-ring]]). Let
$U_R:=U_A\otimes_AR$ be the base
change of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], identified with its image in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

(a) **Halves.** Each root component $U_R^\pm[\pm\nu]$ is a finite free
$R$-module, generated as an $R$-module by ordinary words
$E_{i_1}\cdots E_{i_k}$ (respectively $F_{i_1}\cdots F_{i_k}$) of degree
$\pm\nu$, and its $q=1$ fibre $U_R^\pm[\pm\nu]\otimes_RR/(q-1)$ is the classical
half $U(\mathfrak n^\pm)_{\mathbb Q}[\pm\nu]$ of the Kac-Moody algebra,
presented by the separate classical Serre relations
([[thm-generic-quantum-serre-halves-have-classical-pbw-ranks-and-a-nondegenerate-hopf-pairing]](i),
[[thm-serre-presentation-of-a-kac-moody-algebra]]).

(b) **Torus.** Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and let $L=\sum_i\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)$.
Then $U_R^0$ has the $R$-basis
$\{K_c\prod_iK_i^{\delta_i}H_i^{t_i}\}$ with $\delta_i\in\{0,1\}$,
$t_i\ge0$ and $c$ running through the explicit representatives of
$P^{\vee}/L$ of
[[lem-unmodified-integral-torus-has-a-quantum-binomial-basis]](b); and
multiplication
$U_R^-\otimes_RU_R^0\otimes_RU_R^+\to U_R$ is an isomorphism of
$R$-modules.

(c) **Positive quotient.** For every characteristic-zero field $k$ (an
$A$-algebra via $q\mapsto1$), the positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra $k[H_i:i\in I]$
with, in it, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$; and the positive full quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$,
where $\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ is the classical Lie algebra presented by the
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots. This is an assertion about the
stated quotient only: it is not claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$, where genuine toral characters such as
$K=-1$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ survive. Direct substitution $q=1$ into the
vanishing denominators $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a minimal realization $(\mathfrak h,(h_i),(\alpha_i))$ of a finite GCM $A$, with the row-coroot convention $\alpha_j(h_i)=a_{ij}$ from [[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]]. Define

$$P=\{\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*: \lambda(h_i)\in\mathbb Z\text{ for every }i\},\qquad P^+=\{\lambda\in P:\lambda(h_i)\geq0\text{ for every }i\}.$$

Elements of $P$ are **integral weights**; elements of $P^+$ are **dominant integral weights**. Their simple-coroot labels are the integers $\lambda(h_i)$. Zero labels are allowed, and the zero functional is dominant integral.

The independent coroots can be extended to a finite basis of $\mathfrak h$. Prescribing integral labels on the coroots and arbitrary complex values on the remaining basis vectors specifies a unique functional. Thus complementary Cartan values are unrestricted; $P$ need not be a discrete lattice in $\mathfrak h^*$. The inequalities only concern the integral coroot labels, not an ordering of arbitrary complex Cartan values. This definition uses finite linear algebra and no AC.

Let $\mathfrak g(A)$ be the algebra of [[def-kac-moody-algebra-associated-to-a-gcm]], with its simple generators $e_i,f_i$ and Cartan $\mathfrak h$. A module $V$ is **integrable** if it is a weight module and every $e_i,f_i$ acts locally nilpotently. Explicitly,

$$V=\bigoplus_{\mu\in\mathfrak h^*}V_\mu,\qquad V_\mu=\{v:hv=\mu(h)v\text{ for all }h\in\mathfrak h\},$$

and for every index $i$ and vector $v\in V$ there are positive integers $N_e,N_f$, depending on $i,v$, such that $e_i^{N_e}v=0$ and $f_i^{N_f}v=0$.

Only the weight-module convention from [[def-kac-moody-category-o]] is used. Finite-dimensional weight spaces, bounded-above support and finite generation are not part of integrability. Nor is a uniform nilpotence exponent required. The zero module is integrable, taking exponents one on its sole vector. derivations.claim: The algebra-level statement. Part (a) is the toral clause of [[lem-rational-local-quantum-halves-and-torus-specialize-at-q-one]](c): the localized basis $\{K_c\prod_iK_i^{\delta_i}H_i^{t_i}\}$ of $U_A^0$ specializes and is then quotiented by all $K_h-1$, leaving the freely generated polynomial algebra $k[H_i]$, and the integral recursion $T_{c+1,t}=z^tT_{c,t}+K^{-1}z^{-c+t-1}T_{c,t-1}$ with $T_{c,1}=K_i[c]_i+q_i^{-c}T_{i,0,1}$ specializes to the Pascal recursion with value $\binom{H_i+c}{t}$; the kernel of $U_A^0\otimes_Ak\twoheadrightarrow k[H_i]$ is exactly $(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$. Nothing here is a statement about the unquotiented specialization.

Scalar operators on a label-graded lattice. Let $\mu\in P$ and $x\in M_A\cap M_\mu$. By [F2], $K_hx=q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}x$ and $T_{i,c,t}x=\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}_ix$. Here $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle\in\mathbb Z$ by the integrality of the labels [F3], so the binomial is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$, and after tensoring with $k$ its value is the integer $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$ of [F3]; the scalar $q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle}$ specializes to $1$. Since $M_A=\bigoplus_\mu(M_A\cap M_\mu)$ by the grading hypothesis, these piecewise scalars define honest operators on all of $M_A\otimes_Ak$: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$ and $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acting by $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$ on the image of each piece. In particular these scalar operators are integer-valued, and $\bar H_i$ acts by $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$. If the lattice is not graded in this sense, a general lattice element may have weight components outside $M_A$ and the scalar operators need not descend; this is the caveat of the statement.

The classical Cartan commutators. All generators $E_i,F_j,H_i,K_h$ preserve $M_A$ by [F2], so the integral operator identities descend to $M_A\otimes_Ak$. The mixed relation gives $\bar E_i\bar F_j-\bar F_j\bar E_i=\delta_{ij}\bar T_{i,0,1}=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$; the shifted toral relations give $\bar H_i\bar E_j=\bar E_j\binom{\bar H_i+a_{ij}}{1}=\bar E_j(\bar H_i+a_{ij})$ and $\bar H_i\bar F_j=\bar F_j(\bar H_i-a_{ij})$, because on the image of $M_A\cap M_\mu$ both sides act by the scalars $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$ resp. $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+a_{ij}$ and $T_{i,a_{ij},1}$ specializes to $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+a_{ij}}{1}=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+a_{ij}$ by step 1.2. Hence the specialized operators satisfy the classical Cartan commutators of (b). No step divides by $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ after specializing. The factors $[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$ are units in the local DVR; quantum-integer and binomial ratios are evaluated through their Laurent-polynomial identities, not by treating the vanishing $q_i-q_i^{-1}$ as a unit.
