Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral, so $m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$
for all $i$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with highest vector
$v_\lambda$ ([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]).
Put $s_i:=F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$.

(i) Every $s_i$ is a singular (highest weight) vector of weight
$\lambda-(m_i+1)\alpha_i$.

(ii) The graded submodule
$S:=\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)s_i=\sum_iU_q^-s_i$ is proper, and the quotient
$\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/S$ is nonzero, has finite-dimensional
label-weight spaces, and is integrable ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]).

(iii) Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of highest weight
$\lambda$ is a quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$.

No commutation between divided powers $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$ of distinct indices
with $a_{ij}\ne0$ is assumed anywhere.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight and let
$\tilde L(\lambda)$ be the nonzero integrable quotient of the Verma module
$M(\lambda)$ of [[lem-quantum-highest-weight-serre-quotient-is-integrable]]
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), with
highest vector $v_\lambda$ and label grading
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]). Put
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$.

(a) **Character.** Every nonzero graded quotient $V$ of $\tilde L(\lambda)$
whose highest line is nonzero is generated by its highest vector and has in
every label the same dimension as the classical simple integrable highest
weight module of the regularized minimal realization of the same Cartan datum
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]],
[[thm-kac-moody-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]); in particular the
character is independent of $V$. No global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and
no crystal or global basis is used.

(b) **Uniqueness.** Consequently $\tilde L(\lambda)$ is simple, hence is the
canonical simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$, and every integrable cyclic
highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ is a quotient of
$L(\lambda)$.

(c) **The $R$-lattice.** For a nonzero highest vector $v$ of $V$, the lattice
$V_R:=\sum_wR\,F_wv$, summed over all ordinary words $w$ in the negative
generators, is stable under every generator of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], is finite free over $R$ on each
label weight, and is generated by $v$ under $U_A$ after extension to $R$; its $q=1$ fibre
$V_R/(q-1)V_R$ is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the
regularized minimal realization. Here the Gaussian binomials
$\binom{m}{r}_i$ of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]
are $R$-valued at integer labels, and the divided-power denominators
$[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$ are $R$-units.

Let $\lambda\in P$, let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with its canonical
$P$-label grading and highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), and let
$\sigma$ be the linear contravariant anti-involution of
[[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]
($\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$,
$\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$).

(i) **Existence and uniqueness.** Define the $\lambda$-weight functional
$\eta\colon U_q(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by $\eta(y):=$ the coefficient of
$v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$ (so $\eta(y)$ is unchanged by adding an element of
the Verma ideal $J(\lambda)$, and $\eta(1)=1$). Then
$$B\bigl(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda\bigr):=\eta\bigl(\sigma(a)b\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in U_q^-)$$
is a well-defined bilinear form on $M(\lambda)$; it is homogeneous, normalized
($B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$) and $\sigma$-contravariant,
$B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$. It is the unique such form on $M(\lambda)$, in the
sense of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(ii) **Radical and descent.** The radical
$\operatorname{rad}B=\{u:B(u,M(\lambda))=0\}$ equals the sum $N(\lambda)$ of all
proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$; consequently $B$ descends to a
nondegenerate normalized $\sigma$-contravariant form on the simple highest
weight quotient $L(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$.

(iii) **Rank-one norms and dominant singular vectors.** If
$m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ (that is, $\lambda$ dominant), then for
every $r\ge0$
$$B\bigl(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda\bigr)=q_i^{\,r(m_i-r)}\binom{m_i}{r}_i,$$
with the Gaussian binomial interpreted as $0$ for $r>m_i$; in particular each
$F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$ lies in the radical, so $B$ factors through the Serre
quotient $M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$. (The same
computation proves the norm formula for every $\lambda$ and all $r$ for which
the right-hand side is read with $m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$.)

(iv) **Ordinary simplicity.** Let $V$ be an integrable cyclic graded quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ with support in $\lambda-Q_+$ on which the descended form is
nondegenerate. Then $V$ is simple as an ordinary module (not only as a graded
module).

(v) **Integrality of the lattice values.** If $\lambda$ is integral and
$V_A:=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda\subseteq L(\lambda)$ is the highest lattice of
the Lusztig form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), then
$B(V_A,V_A)\subseteq A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ is
asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with Borel subalgebra
$U_q^{\ge0}=U_q^0U_q^+$ and negative half $U_q^-$
([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]). Fix
$\lambda\in P$ and let $\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)$ be the
**Borel character module** on which $K_h$ acts by the scalar
$q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}$ and every $E_i$ acts as $0$ (the character is a
well-defined $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism
$\chi_\lambda\colon U_q^{\ge0}\to\mathbb Q(q)$, Verification, step 1.1). The
**quantum Verma module** is the induced module

$$M(\lambda):=U_q(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{U_q^{\ge0}}\mathbb Q(q)_\lambda,$$

a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module, with distinguished vector
$v_\lambda:=1\otimes1$ ([[def-quotient-ring]] for the quotient/induction
conventions).

Then (Verification, steps 2.1 and 3.1):

(i) $M(\lambda)$ carries the **canonical $P$-label grading**
$M(\lambda)=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M(\lambda)_\mu$ with
$M(\lambda)_{\lambda-\nu}=U_q^-[-\nu]v_\lambda$ for $\nu\in Q_+$ and
$M(\lambda)_\mu=0$ otherwise; each $M(\lambda)_\mu$ is finite dimensional
(there are only finitely many words in the $F_i$ of a given root degree), and
$M(\lambda)_\lambda=\mathbb Q(q)v_\lambda$ is the highest line. With this
grading $M(\lambda)$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) and $v_\lambda$ is a highest
weight vector: $K_hv_\lambda=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v_\lambda$,
$E_iv_\lambda=0$, $M(\lambda)=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.

(ii) (Universal property) For every left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $V$ and every
$v\in V$ with $K_hv=q^{\langle\lambda,h\rangle}v$ and $E_iv=0$ for all $h,i$
there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with
$v_\lambda\mapsto v$; if $V=U_q(\mathfrak g)v$ is cyclic, this map is
surjective. When $V$ is a $P$-graded type-one module and $v\in V_\lambda$, the
map is grading-preserving.

(iii) The sum $N(\lambda)$ of all proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$ is a
proper graded submodule, and

$$L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$$

is the **simple highest weight quotient**: it has no nonzero proper graded
submodule, and it is the unique simple graded quotient of $M(\lambda)$ up to
isomorphism ([[def-submodule]]). Thus the maximal proper submodule occurring
here is the sum of *all* proper graded submodules, not an arbitrarily chosen
maximal one; no choice is used.

If the pairing separates $P$, then every submodule of $M(\lambda)$ is graded,
$N(\lambda)$ is the unique maximal proper submodule, and $L(\lambda)$ is the
ordinary simple (not only graded-simple) quotient: this is the usual simple
weight-module quotient of the Verma module over a separating torus
(Verification, step 4.1).

The contravariant Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`
identifies $N(\lambda)$ with the radical of the normalized Verma contravariant
form and gives the canonical normalized form on $L(\lambda)$; for $\lambda$
dominant integral, the existence theorem
`thm-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module-exists-and-is-unique` proves the
ordinary simplicity and the universal integrable conclusions. Both are
declared obligations of those later items, not assumptions here.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: Construction, support and integrability. The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda)$ of the statement is the quotient constructed in [F1] (the sum of the vectors $F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$ and their $U_q$-translates is the displayed submodule); hence it is nonzero, has one-dimensional top label space with generator $\bar v_\lambda\ne0$, has finite-dimensional label weights, support contained in $\lambda-Q_+$, and is integrable. This proves the first part of (i).

Identification with the simple module and character. The simple graded quotient $L(\lambda)$ of $M(\lambda)$ is a nonzero graded quotient of $\tilde L(\lambda)$ with nonzero highest line: the image of $\bar v_\lambda$ generates it, and a nonzero highest vector of weight $\lambda$ cannot lie in the kernel, since the kernel is a graded submodule not containing the top label space. By [F2] both $\tilde L(\lambda)$ and $L(\lambda)$ have the classical simple character, so the surjection $\tilde L(\lambda)\to L(\lambda)$ is injective on every finite-dimensional label space, hence an isomorphism; $\tilde L(\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)$ and the character statement (iii) follow.
Ordinary simplicity. By [F3], $L(\lambda)$ has no proper nonzero ordinary submodule. Since $\tilde L(\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)$, the same holds for $\tilde L(\lambda)$; this completes (i).

Universality. Let $V$ be an integrable cyclic highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$. By [F4] there is a unique $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $M(\lambda)\to V$ with $v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and it is surjective because $v$ generates $V$. By [F1](iii) the integrability of $V$ forces this map to kill the defining submodule of $\tilde L(\lambda)$: namely the kernel contains each $F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$, since the image $F_i^{(m_i+1)}v$ must vanish (the minimal $t_i$ with $F_i^{t_i}v=0$ equals $m_i+1$ by the rank-one string computation used in [F1]); hence the map factors through $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$. This map is unique because it is determined on the cyclic vector, and it sends the class of $v_\lambda$ to $v$. If $V\ne0$, then by step 1.3 the source $\tilde L(\lambda)\cong L(\lambda)$ is simple, so the surjection is an isomorphism: $V\cong L(\lambda)$. This proves (ii).

Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 with all nine prerequisite interfaces, especially the fully reviewed Serre quotient, local deformation and Cartan form proofs. Any nonzero integrable cyclic highest module receives the unique highest-vector map and kills the minimal rank-one singular powers; ordinary simplicity makes that surjection an isomorphism. Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight, put
$m_i:=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$, and let $M(\lambda)$ be the quantum Verma
module with highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]],
[[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]).

(i) The quotient $\tilde L(\lambda):=M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$
is nonzero, has finite-dimensional label weights and support contained in
$\lambda-Q_+$, is integrable, and equals the canonical simple highest weight
module $L(\lambda)$, which is simple also as an ordinary (not assumed graded)
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module.

(ii) **Universality.** Every integrable cyclic highest weight module $V$ of
highest weight $\lambda$ with highest vector $v\ne0$ receives a
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module map $\tilde L(\lambda)\to V$ with
$\bar v_\lambda\mapsto v$, and this map is unique; every nonzero such $V$ is
isomorphic to $L(\lambda)$.

(iii) Its character equals the classical integrable highest weight character of
the explicitly regularized realization of the datum. No global
$\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and no crystal or global basis is used.

Let $\lambda\in P$, let $M(\lambda)$ be the Verma module with its canonical
$P$-label grading and highest vector $v_\lambda$
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), and let
$\sigma$ be the linear contravariant anti-involution of
[[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]]
($\sigma(K_h)=K_h$, $\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1}$,
$\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i$).

(i) **Existence and uniqueness.** Define the $\lambda$-weight functional
$\eta\colon U_q(\mathfrak g)\to\mathbb Q(q)$ by $\eta(y):=$ the coefficient of
$v_\lambda$ in $yv_\lambda$ (so $\eta(y)$ is unchanged by adding an element of
the Verma ideal $J(\lambda)$, and $\eta(1)=1$). Then
$$B\bigl(av_\lambda,bv_\lambda\bigr):=\eta\bigl(\sigma(a)b\bigr)\qquad(a,b\in U_q^-)$$
is a well-defined bilinear form on $M(\lambda)$; it is homogeneous, normalized
($B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$) and $\sigma$-contravariant,
$B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$. It is the unique such form on $M(\lambda)$, in the
sense of [[def-contravariant-form-on-an-integrable-quantum-highest-weight-module]].

(ii) **Radical and descent.** The radical
$\operatorname{rad}B=\{u:B(u,M(\lambda))=0\}$ equals the sum $N(\lambda)$ of all
proper graded submodules of $M(\lambda)$; consequently $B$ descends to a
nondegenerate normalized $\sigma$-contravariant form on the simple highest
weight quotient $L(\lambda)=M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$.

(iii) **Rank-one norms and dominant singular vectors.** If
$m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ (that is, $\lambda$ dominant), then for
every $r\ge0$
$$B\bigl(F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda,F_i^{(r)}v_\lambda\bigr)=q_i^{\,r(m_i-r)}\binom{m_i}{r}_i,$$
with the Gaussian binomial interpreted as $0$ for $r>m_i$; in particular each
$F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$ lies in the radical, so $B$ factors through the Serre
quotient $M(\lambda)/\sum_iU_q(\mathfrak g)F_i^{(m_i+1)}v_\lambda$. (The same
computation proves the norm formula for every $\lambda$ and all $r$ for which
the right-hand side is read with $m_i=\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle$.)

(iv) **Ordinary simplicity.** Let $V$ be an integrable cyclic graded quotient of
$M(\lambda)$ with support in $\lambda-Q_+$ on which the descended form is
nondegenerate. Then $V$ is simple as an ordinary module (not only as a graded
module).

(v) **Integrality of the lattice values.** If $\lambda$ is integral and
$V_A:=U_Av_\lambda=U_A^-v_\lambda\subseteq L(\lambda)$ is the highest lattice of
the Lusztig form ([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]), then
$B(V_A,V_A)\subseteq A=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$. No perfectness of $B$ over $A$ is
asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The **linear
contravariant anti-involution** $\sigma$ of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ is defined on
generators by

$$\sigma(q)=q,\qquad\sigma(K_h)=K_h,\qquad\sigma(E_i)=q_iF_iK_i^{-1},\qquad\sigma(F_i)=q_i^{-1}K_iE_i,$$

extended as an anti-algebra map, $\sigma(xy)=\sigma(y)\sigma(x)$. It is
$\mathbb Q(q)$-linear, preserves the torus (it does not invert it), and is an
involution (Verification, step 1.1). It is distinct from the semilinear
contravariant anti-involution $\tau$ with $\tau(q)=q^{-1}$,
$\tau(E_i)=F_i$, $\tau(F_i)=E_i$, $\tau(K_h)=K_{-h}$ of
[[lem-quantum-serre-relations-are-stable-under-the-chevalley-involutions]].

Let $\lambda\in P$ be dominant integral ([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]),
so $\langle\lambda,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for all $i$, and let $(M,v_\lambda)$ be a
**normalized highest weight module**: $M$ is a $P$-graded type-one quantum
weight module ([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) with
$v_\lambda\in M_\lambda$, $E_iv_\lambda=0$ for all $i$, and $M=U_q(\mathfrak g)v_\lambda$.
(The normalized simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$ is the companion
construction later on this page; the present definition applies to any
normalized highest weight module, in particular to the Verma module and to its
simple quotient.)

A **contravariant form** on $(M,v_\lambda)$ is a bilinear form
$B\colon M\times M\to\mathbb Q(q)$ such that

(i) $B$ is symmetric: $B(u,v)=B(v,u)$ for all $u,v\in M$;

(ii) $B$ is **homogeneous** for the label grading: $B(M_\mu,M_\tau)=0$
whenever the two labels have different toral characters, that is, whenever
$\langle\mu,h\rangle\ne\langle\tau,h\rangle$ for some $h\in P^{\vee}$;

(iii) $B(v_\lambda,v_\lambda)=1$ (the normalization);

(iv) $B$ is $\sigma$-invariant: $B(xu,v)=B(u,\sigma(x)v)$ for all
$x\in U_q(\mathfrak g)$ and all $u,v\in M$.

Because $\sigma$ is $\mathbb Q(q)$-linear and fixes the torus, condition (iv)
is equivalent to the adjunction displays

$$B(K_hu,v)=B(u,K_hv),\qquad B(E_iu,v)=B(u,q_iF_iK_i^{-1}v),\qquad B(F_iu,v)=B(u,q_i^{-1}K_iE_iv),$$

for all $u,v\in M$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$ (Verification, step 2.1).

For $\lambda$ dominant and $L(\lambda)$ the normalized simple highest weight
module, such a form exists, is unique, and is nondegenerate on $L(\lambda)$;
moreover distinct label-weight spaces with distinct characters are orthogonal
by (ii). Uniqueness is proved here (Verification, step 2.2), as is the
orthogonality; consequently, when the pairing separates $P$, the distinct
label-weight spaces of $L(\lambda)$ are orthogonal and the restriction of $B$
to each finite-dimensional label-weight space is nondegenerate (Verification,
step 4.1). The
existence, the identification of the radical on the Verma module and the
descent to $L(\lambda)$ are proved in the local Cartan-projection lemma
`lem-cartan-projection-constructs-the-quantum-verma-contravariant-form`, which
is the declared justification of this definition. That lemma is proved on this
page, and its statement is the supplier of the existence and nondegeneracy
clauses above; establishing those clauses is its content rather than a claim of
this definition.

Let $M$ be a left $R$-module. A subset $N\subseteq M$ is a **submodule** when
it is a subgroup of the additive group of $M$ and is closed under scalars:

$$r\in R,\ n\in N\quad\Longrightarrow\quad rn\in N.$$

The operations on $N$ are the restrictions of those of $M$. Write $N\le M$ when
the ring and module are understood.

([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,

$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum with $a_{ii}=2$ for
all $i$ ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and let $M$ be a
$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]) whose support is contained in
a finite union of cones,

$$\operatorname{supp}M\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^{s}(\lambda_j-Q_+)\qquad(\lambda_1,\dots,\lambda_s\in P),$$

where $Q_+=\bigoplus_i\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\alpha_i$. Choose a finite free direct
coordinate summand $X_f\subseteq P$ (with respect to a free basis of $P$,
[[def-free-abelian-group]]) containing all $\lambda_j$ and all $\alpha_i$, and
set

$$Y_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\Bigl(\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb ZH_i\Bigr)\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z),\qquad X_{\mathrm{aux}}:=\operatorname{Hom}(Y_{\mathrm{aux}},\mathbb Z),$$

with the evaluation pairing $X_{\mathrm{aux}}\times Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\to\mathbb Z$.
Define $j\colon X_f\to X_{\mathrm{aux}}$ by $j(x)(H_i):=\langle x,h_i\rangle$ and
$j(x)(f):=f(x)$ for $f\in\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)$, and put
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}:=j(\alpha_i)$. Then:

(i) $(I,A,D,X_{\mathrm{aux}},Y_{\mathrm{aux}},q)$ with the simple roots
$\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ and simple coroots $H_i$ is a symmetrizable Cartan
datum for a quantum group with the same generalized Cartan matrix $A$ and the
same symmetrizer $D$; its pairing is perfect, the $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$ are
linearly independent, the $H_i$ are primitive and independent, and integral
fundamental weights $\Lambda_j$ ($\Lambda_j(H_i)=\delta_{ij}$) exist. Here
$\langle\alpha_j^{\mathrm{aux}},H_i\rangle=a_{ij}$ is the original convention
([[def-realization-of-a-generalized-cartan-matrix]],
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]]).

(ii) Fix the transported $X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-grading
$$M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{j(x)}:=M_x\quad(x\in X_f),\qquad M^{\mathrm{aux}}_{\xi}:=0\quad(\xi\notin j(X_f)),$$
so $\operatorname{supp}M^{\mathrm{aux}}\subseteq j(X_f)$. On this fixed graded
space there is a unique type-one quantum weight module structure for the
auxiliary datum retaining the original $E_i,F_i$ actions: its toral action is
$$K_{(n,f)}\ \text{acts on}\ M_x\ \text{by}\ q^{\sum_in_i\langle x,h_i\rangle+f(x)}\qquad\bigl((n,f)\in\textstyle\bigoplus_i\mathbb ZH_i\oplus\operatorname{Hom}(X_f,\mathbb Z)\bigr),$$
with the actions of $E_i$, $F_i$ and of the simple coroots
$K_{d_iH_i}$ unchanged. In particular the old $K_h$ action is recovered from
the label $x$ as $q^{\langle x,h\rangle}$, and the old and auxiliary $E_i,F_i$
actions agree.
Uniqueness is asserted for this transported grading; the original toral action
alone need not determine the labels when the original pairing is not separating.

(iii) The two recipes are inverse on objects and grading-preserving morphisms:
on $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-modules with labels in $X_f$ and support as above, the
identity on underlying vector spaces is an equivalence between the category of
$P$-graded type-one modules and the corresponding full subcategory of
$X_{\mathrm{aux}}$-graded type-one modules with labels in $j(X_f)$. This is not
an embedding of the old torus algebra into the new one and is asserted only
inside this finite-support category.

(iv) The construction applies simultaneously to Verma modules and highest weight
modules (supported in $\lambda-Q_+$) and to finite tensor products of such
modules (labels add), by choosing one $X_f$ containing all participating upper
weights and all simple roots; the tensor-product $E_i,F_i$ formulas of [[thm-the-drinfeld-jimbo-formulas-define-a-hopf-algebra]] are unchanged because only the diagonal toral characters change.

(v) Rationally, $h_{\mathrm{aux}}:=Y_{\mathrm{aux}}\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$
decomposes as $h_{\mathrm{aux}}=H_{\min}\oplus Z$, where $H_{\min}$ is a
minimal realization of $A$ (of dimension $2n-r$, $n=|I|$, $r=\operatorname{rank}A$)
and $Z\subseteq\ker\alpha$ is a complement on which all $\alpha_i^{\mathrm{aux}}$
vanish. After extension to $\mathbb C$, $H_{\min}\otimes\mathbb C$ is a
minimal realization in the sense of
[[prop-minimal-realizations-exist-and-are-unique-up-to-isomorphism]], and the
extended Cartan–Serre algebra is $\mathfrak g(H_{\min}\otimes\mathbb C)\oplus
(Z\otimes\mathbb C)$. For a classical highest weight module with highest
weight $\xi$, the central summand acts by $\xi|_Z$; restriction to the minimal
realization preserves its submodules and its weight multiplicities, with
$\xi-\nu$ indexed by the same $\nu\in Q_+$.

Let $\lambda\in P$ be a dominant integral label weight and let
$\tilde L(\lambda)$ be the nonzero integrable quotient of the Verma module
$M(\lambda)$ of [[lem-quantum-highest-weight-serre-quotient-is-integrable]]
([[def-quantum-verma-module-and-simple-highest-weight-quotient]]), with
highest vector $v_\lambda$ and label grading
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]). Put
$R:=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}\subset\mathbb Q(q)$.

(a) **Character.** Every nonzero graded quotient $V$ of $\tilde L(\lambda)$
whose highest line is nonzero is generated by its highest vector and has in
every label the same dimension as the classical simple integrable highest
weight module of the regularized minimal realization of the same Cartan datum
([[lem-finite-support-regularization-of-quantum-label-weight-modules]],
[[thm-kac-moody-verma-module-has-a-unique-simple-quotient]]); in particular the
character is independent of $V$. No global $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$-freeness and
no crystal or global basis is used.

(b) **Uniqueness.** Consequently $\tilde L(\lambda)$ is simple, hence is the
canonical simple highest weight module $L(\lambda)$, and every integrable cyclic
highest weight module of highest weight $\lambda$ is a quotient of
$L(\lambda)$.

(c) **The $R$-lattice.** For a nonzero highest vector $v$ of $V$, the lattice
$V_R:=\sum_wR\,F_wv$, summed over all ordinary words $w$ in the negative
generators, is stable under every generator of the integral form $U_A$ of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]], is finite free over $R$ on each
label weight, and is generated by $v$ under $U_A$ after extension to $R$; its $q=1$ fibre
$V_R/(q-1)V_R$ is the classical simple integrable highest weight module of the
regularized minimal realization. Here the Gaussian binomials
$\binom{m}{r}_i$ of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]
are $R$-valued at integer labels, and the divided-power denominators
$[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$ are $R$-units.

Let $R$ be a unital ring and $(M_i)_{i\in I}$ a family of left $R$-modules ([[def-left-and-right-modules]]). Their **direct product** is the module $\prod_{i\in I}M_i$ with coordinatewise operations. The **support** of $m=(m_i)$ is $\{i\in I:m_i\ne0\}$, and the **direct sum** is the submodule
$$\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i=\{m\in\prod_{i\in I}M_i:\operatorname{supp}(m)\text{ is finite}\}$$
([[def-submodule]]).

This subset is a submodule because the support of a sum is contained in the union of two finite supports and scalar multiplication cannot enlarge support.

For each $i$, the coordinate inclusion $\jmath_i:M_i\to\bigoplus_jM_j$ puts its input in coordinate $i$ and zero elsewhere. If $I=\varnothing$, both product and direct sum are the zero module.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Finite rank-one reduction. For homogeneous $x$, choose $N\ge1$ with $E_i^Nx=0$ and put $W_x:=\operatorname{span}\{F_i^{(a)}E_i^bx:0\le b<N,\ a\ge0\}$. Local nilpotence of $F_i$ on each of the finitely many $E_i^bx$ makes this span finite. The divided commutation formula of [F1] proves $E_i$ preserves it, while $F_i$ and $K_i^{\pm1}$ preserve it directly. Thus $W_x$ is a finite-dimensional type-one $A_i$-module, with $E_i,F_i$ nilpotent and $K_i$ diagonalizable; its labels lie on the single line through $\mathrm{wt}(x)$. A general vector has finite label support, so it too lies in a finite sum of such modules.

Finite rank-one strings, proved locally. In a finite-dimensional type-one $A_i$-module, a nonzero $E_i$-highest eigenvector $y$ of integer weight $a$ has a minimal $t\ge1$ with $F_i^{(t)}y=0$. Applying $E_i$ and [F1] gives $[a-t+1]_iF_i^{(t-1)}y=0$, hence $t=a+1$ and $a\ge0$; the positions $F_i^{(n)}y$, $0\le n\le a$, are nonzero and have distinct $K_i$-eigenvalues. Each simple composition factor has such a vector (take an eigencomponent of a last nonzero $E_i$-iterate), whose string is a nonzero submodule and therefore the entire factor. Put $C:=F_iE_i+(q_iK_i+q_i^{-1}K_i^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$. The relations of [F1] give $[C,E_i]=[C,F_i]=[C,K_i]=0$, and $C$ acts on a highest string of weight $a$ by $c_a=(q_i^{a+1}+q_i^{-a-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})^2$. These scalars are distinct for $a\ge0$: equality factors as $(q_i^{a+1}-q_i^{b+1})(1-q_i^{-a-b-2})=0$, forcing $a=b$. Split a finite module into its generalized $C$-eigenspaces. In the $c_a$-block all composition factors are strings of highest weight $a$, so if their number is $k$, the $K_i$-weight spaces $a,a-2,\ldots,-a$ all have dimension $k$ and there are no other weights. Its top space is killed by $E_i$; the maps $F_i^{(n)}$ on that space are injective for $n\le a$ by the first endpoint argument and vanish for $n>a$. Their images therefore exhaust the block's distinct weight spaces. This proves the finite string decomposition without assuming rank-one complete reducibility. Applied to $W_x$, the tops and positions have the chosen labels: on its single root line, the $K_i$-eigenvalue determines the label since $\langle\alpha_i,h_i\rangle=2$.

Positive spans and restricted-dual integrability. The labels of $U^{\ge0}x$ lie above one of the finitely many labels of $x$ and below one of the finitely many upper labels $\lambda_j$. Each interval contains finitely many labels because the simple roots freely generate $Q$, and each label space is finite-dimensional, so $U^{\ge0}x$ is finite-dimensional. Fix $\mu,i$ and an integer $T\ge0$ with $M_{\mu+t\alpha_i}=0$ for all integers $t>T$; such a bound follows from the $\alpha_i$ coefficient in each possible expression $\lambda_j-\mu-t\alpha_i\in Q_+$. Put $a=\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$. By step 2.1, any vector on this line is a sum of positions of strings whose top is $\mu+t\alpha_i$ with $t\le T$, highest integer $a+2t\ge0$ and position $0\le n\le a+2t$. The position label $\mu+(t-n)\alpha_i$ satisfies $-a-T\le t-n\le T$. Thus the line has finite support. Under [F4], $E_i$ raises and $F_i$ lowers a functional's support by $\alpha_i$; both sufficiently high powers vanish for a functional at $\mu$. Finite maxima over its finite label support prove that $M^*$, and the restricted dual of any graded submodule with the same upper bound, is integrable. No global coroot bound is used.

Maximal vectors. Let $F\subseteq M$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional graded $U^{\ge0}$-stable subspace and choose a maximal label $\mu$ in its finite support. Pick $0\ne v_\mu\in F_\mu$. Since $F_{\mu+\alpha_i}=0$ for each $i$, every $E_i$ kills $v_\mu$. Step 2.1 applied in its finite rank-one module gives $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle\ge0$ for every $i$, so $\mu\in P^+$. The cyclic module $L:=U_qv_\mu$ is integrable and isomorphic to the ordinary-simple $L(\mu)$ by [F3].

The duality retraction. Put $N:=U_qF=U_q^-F$. Its support lies in the finite union $\bigcup_{\nu\in\mathrm{wt}(F)}(\nu-Q_+)$; maximality of $\mu$ implies $N_{\mu+\alpha_i}=0$ for each $i$ and $N_\mu=F_\mu$, without requiring the other maximal labels to lie below $\mu$. Choose $\psi\in(N_\mu)^*$ with $\psi(v_\mu)=1$ and extend it by zero on the other labels. Since $\sigma(E_i)$ lowers a label by $\alpha_i$, $E_i\psi=0$. By step 3.1, the whole restricted dual $N^*$ is integrable, so $W:=U_q\psi$ is the integrable highest module $L(\mu)$ by [F3]. Evaluation gives a grading-preserving module map $\Phi:N\to W^*_{\mathrm{res}}$, with $\Phi(x)(w)=w(x)$: a finite-label vector $x$ defines a finite-label functional, and invariance follows from [F4]. The homogeneous nondegenerate contravariant form on $W$ identifies $W$ with its restricted dual on each finite-dimensional label space. Choose the unique normalized highest-vector isomorphism $W\cong L$ and rescale the composite so that $\pi(v_\mu)=v_\mu$; this is possible since evaluation on $(v_\mu,\psi)$ is $1$. The grading-preserving module map $\pi:N\to L$ restricts to the identity on the cyclic simple $L$, hence $N=L\oplus\ker\pi$.

Finite induction. For the graded $F$ of steps 3.2 and 4.1 put $G:=(\mathrm{id}-\pi)F$. The grading-preserving retraction makes $G$ graded, finite-dimensional and $U^{\ge0}$-stable, and $U_qG=\ker\pi$. Since $v_\mu\in F\cap L$ is killed by $\mathrm{id}-\pi$, $\dim G<\dim F$. Induction on $\dim F$ therefore decomposes $U_qF$ as a finite direct sum of simple highest modules. This also covers an arbitrary finite-dimensional $U^{\ge0}$-stable generating space $F_0$: its finite graded hull $F$ is stable by [F5], and $U_qF_0$ is an ordinary submodule of the finite direct sum $U_qF$. Every submodule of a finite direct sum of ordinary simple modules is itself a finite direct sum of simples: induct on the number of summands, splitting off the first summand if it is contained in the submodule, and otherwise inject the submodule into the remaining summands by projection. Each resulting simple is isomorphic to a summand by a nonzero coordinate projection. This argument uses only finite choices.

The general module. For $x\in M$, the finite graded hull of $U^{\ge0}x$ is finite and stable by step 3.1 and [F5], so step 5.1 places $x$ in a finite sum of ordinary-simple highest modules. Hence $M$ is a sum of simple submodules. By AC choose a maximal independent family in the set of simple submodules; an ordinary simple not contained in its sum has zero intersection with that sum and would enlarge the family, so maximality gives $M=\bigoplus_\alpha S_\alpha$. Every $S_\alpha$ is isomorphic to some $L(\lambda)$ by a nonzero coordinate projection to one of the finite highest-module sums containing a nonzero vector of $S_\alpha$. For a nonzero ordinary submodule $V\subseteq M$, choose $0\ne x\in V$ and a finite simple sum containing $x$. Its intersection with $V$ is a nonzero submodule of that finite sum, so step 5.1 gives a simple highest-module copy inside $V$; the image of its highest vector is a maximal vector whose cyclic submodule is that copy. This proves the concrete clause as an ordinary-module assertion, without assuming an ordinary submodule respects the chosen label grading. The original finite label grading and [F6] retain the datum convention throughout. AC occurs only at the maximal-family step; all finite generated cases were choice-free.

boundaries.evidence: The statement includes the zero module; step 5.1 uses induction on the finite generating dimension and step 6.1 permits the empty independent family, yielding the zero direct sum.
The finite induction of step 5.1 terminates at zero generating dimension; the zero module has the empty decomposition in the statement and step 6.1.
Step 3.2 constructs one simple highest module from a maximal top vector, and step 4.1 retracts onto that copy; step 5.1 handles a single-copy finite generating case.

Step 3.1 uses finite support on each fixed simple-root line instead of a global coroot bound; steps 4.1 and 5.1 allow incomparable upper labels and ordinary submodules that need not respect the chosen grading.
Step 2.1 proves the rank-one endpoint t=a+1; step 3.1 bounds each fixed-line position between -a-T and T, which gives both transpose local-nilpotence endpoints.
AC selects a maximal independent family of simple submodules in step 6.1; the finite graded hull, duality retraction and finite induction of steps 4.1 and 5.1 require only finite choices.

boundaries.reason: The proposition asserts a decomposition rather than a biconditional; step 5.1 proves the finite generated case and step 6.1 proves the general algebraic direct sum.
No converse implication is stated; step 6.1 proves the concrete maximal-vector clause by intersecting an ordinary submodule with a finite simple sum.

risk_review.notes: Accepted the reader's Berkeley source correction, and amended the title to include finite-dimensional weight spaces, matching Statement (a); refuter:5:1 is confirmed fatal as an unsupported broader advertised scope. Read Statement/Facts/Proof 1.1–6.1 and all fourteen dependency interfaces. Finite rank-one cyclic hulls are stable; the explicit central rank-one Casimir separates highest integer strings and proves their finite complete reducibility locally. Finite upper cones and finite label dimensions make positive cyclic spans finite; the top bound and rank-one symmetry bound both ends of each fixed simple-root line, making the restricted sigma-dual integrable. A maximal label in a finite graded Borel-stable generating space supplies a simple highest submodule; evaluation against its normalized highest dual vector and the homogeneous nondegenerate form yield a grading-preserving retraction. Dimension induction splits the finite generated case; finite simple-sum submodule induction also covers ordinary ungraded submodules. The arbitrary module is a sum of these finite sums, and AC selects a maximal independent family only in the final step. Zero modules give the empty sum; incomparable maximal labels do not affect the retraction. All finite-cone and finite-weight hypotheses of the actual proof are retained. Berkeley Theorem 13.2.1.10 and Corollary 13.2.1.11 pp.317–318 were read through their proofs and support finite-type background, not the full local statement.

For a finite symmetrizable GCM over $\mathbb C$, $\mathfrak r^\pm$ is the ideal of the free half $\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^\pm$ generated by $(\operatorname{ad}e_i)^{1-a_{ij}}e_j$ or $(\operatorname{ad}f_i)^{1-a_{ij}}f_j$, respectively, for $i\ne j$. Hence $\mathfrak g(A)$ has exactly the Cartan relations and both Serre families as a presentation. Its halves have the corresponding separate Serre presentations, and multiplication gives the vector-space isomorphism $U(\mathfrak n^-)\otimes U(\mathfrak h)\otimes U(\mathfrak n^+)\cong U(\mathfrak g)$.

Let $R=\mathbb C\llbracket\hbar\rrbracket$, $K=\mathbb C((\hbar))$, $q=e^\hbar$, and $q_i=e^{d_i\hbar}$ for a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum. Let $H^+=U_\hbar\mathfrak n^+$, $\langle V\rangle$ and the shuffle product be as in [[def-formal-quantum-shuffle-borel-for-a-symmetrizable-cartan-datum]], and put $H^-=T(V^*)/J_-$ using [[lem-quantum-serre-sums-vanish-in-the-formal-quantum-shuffle-algebra]]. Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), used only through the formal embedding theorem. For an indeterminate $z$, let $H_z^\pm$ be the algebras over $\mathbb C(z)$ presented by the separate symmetric quantum Serre relations, with parameters $z_i=z^{d_i}$.

(i) Each $H^\pm[\pm\alpha]$ is finite free over $R$, and
$$\operatorname{rank}_R H^\pm[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C}U(\mathfrak n^\pm)[\pm\alpha]=\dim_{\mathbb C(z)}H_z^\pm[\pm\alpha].$$
Every family of homogeneous lifts of a basis of the classical component is an $R$-basis. Likewise, homogeneous word expressions with coefficients rational in $z$, regular at $z=1$, which reduce to a classical component basis form a basis of the corresponding generic component. In particular, for a supplied ordered homogeneous basis of $\mathfrak n^\pm$, ordered monomials in any such regular lifts form a generic PBW basis.

(ii) Both formal halves are graded braided Hopf algebras. Their generators are primitive, their counits kill positive height, and their tensor squares use
$$ (u\otimes v)(u'\otimes v')=q^{-\langle\deg u',\deg v\rangle}uu'\otimes vv',\qquad \langle\epsilon_i,\epsilon_j\rangle=d_i a_{ij},$$
with negative degrees for $H^-$. The word pairing restricts and descends to a nondegenerate $K$-valued pairing $H^+\times H^-$ with $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle=\delta_{ij}/(\hbar d_i)$ and $\langle1,1\rangle=1$. It is zero on unequal opposite degrees and satisfies the braided Hopf adjunctions
$$\langle x,yy'\rangle=\sum\langle x_{(1)},y\rangle\langle x_{(2)},y'\rangle,\qquad\langle xx',y\rangle=\sum\langle x,y_{(1)}\rangle\langle x',y_{(2)}\rangle.$$
The generic halves have the same braided Hopf structures and a nondegenerate $\mathbb C(z)$-valued pairing normalized by $\langle e_i,f_j\rangle_z=\delta_{ij}/(z_i-z_i^{-1})$. Thus opposite graded components are dual. All generic assertions also hold for the corresponding $\mathbb Q(z)$-presentations and their rational pairing, with the PBW lift clause using bases of the rational classical Serre form.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a finite symmetrizable Cartan datum, let
$U_A$ be the integral form with toral part $U_A^0$
([[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]) and let $k$ be a
characteristic-zero field regarded as an $A$-algebra by $q\mapsto1$.
Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and $\bar x$ for the image of $x$ in a specialization.

(a) **Algebra level.** The positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra
$k[H_i:i\in I]$, and in it $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$ for all
$c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$
([[lem-rational-local-quantum-halves-and-torus-specialize-at-q-one]](c)).
No residual $K_h$-ambiguity remains after this quotient — the ideal
$(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is exactly the kernel of the comparison with
$k[H_i]$ — but it is *not* claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A^0\otimes_Ak$.

(b) **Label-graded lattices.** Let $M$ be a $P$-graded type-one
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module with label grading $M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$
([[def-quantum-weight-module-and-integrability]]), and let
$M_A=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}(M_A\cap M_\mu)$ be a $U_A$-stable $A$-submodule that
is graded in the *lattice's own* sense, i.e. it is the direct sum of its
intersections with the label spaces. Then, on $M_A\otimes_Ak$, the operators
induced by $E_i,F_i$ (and all of $U_A$) satisfy: $\bar K_h=\mathrm{id}$ for
every $h\in P^{\vee}$; $\bar T_{i,c,t}$ acts on the image of $M_A\cap M_\mu$ by
the integer $\binom{\langle\mu,h_i\rangle+c}{t}$; and
$[\bar E_i,\bar F_j]=\delta_{ij}\bar H_i$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar E_j]=a_{ij}\bar E_j$,
$[\bar H_i,\bar F_j]=-a_{ij}\bar F_j$, where $\bar H_i$ acts on the image of
$M_A\cap M_\mu$ by the integer $\langle\mu,h_i\rangle$.

The grading hypothesis in (b) is a real hypothesis on the lattice: it is not
inferred from the mere fact that $M_A$ spans a weight module. All divisions
that occur are performed inside the DVR
$R=\mathbb Q[q]_{(q-1)}$ (units $[r]_i!$ and $q_i^{\pm1}$); no vanishing
denominator $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is substituted by $q=1$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum and $i\in I$, and use the conventions of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $C_{m,r}:=\binom{m}{r}_i$, with $C_{m,r}=0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$.

(i) **Pascal recurrences.** For $m\ge1$ and every integer $r$,

$$C_{m,r}=q_i^{-r}C_{m-1,r}+q_i^{m-r}C_{m-1,r-1}=q_i^rC_{m-1,r}+q_i^{r-m}C_{m-1,r-1}.$$

(ii) **Symmetry.** For $0\le r\le m$, $C_{m,r}=C_{m,m-r}$.

(iii) **Gauss product formula.** For every $N\ge0$, in the polynomial ring $\mathbb Q(q)[z]$,

$$\prod_{j=0}^{N-1}(1+q_i^{2j}z)=\sum_{r=0}^{N}q_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}z^r.$$

Consequently, for $N\ge1$,

$$\sum_{r=0}^{N}(-1)^rq_i^{r(N-1)}C_{N,r}=0.$$

(iv) **Integrality.** For $0\le r\le m$,

$$C_{m,r}\in q_i^{-r(m-r)}\mathbb Z[q_i^2]\subseteq\mathbb Z[q_i^{\pm1}].$$

Thus every Gaussian quotient is a Laurent polynomial in $q_i$ with integer coefficients, and the Pascal recurrences hold in that Laurent polynomial ring.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Write $K_i:=K_{d_i h_i}$ and $K_i^{-1}:=K_{-d_i h_i}$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb Q(q)$-vector space with basis the symbols $\{E_i,F_i\}_{i\in I}\cup\{K_h\}_{h\in P^{\vee}}$, and let $T:=T(V)$ be its free unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra ([[def-tensor-algebra-of-a-vector-space]], [[thm-universal-property-of-the-tensor-algebra]]). Let $I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$ be the two-sided ideal of $T$ generated by ([[def-generated-and-principal-ideals]]) the following relations:

$$K_0-1,\qquad K_hK_{h'}-K_{h+h'}\qquad(h,h'\in P^{\vee});$$

$$K_hE_i-q^{\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}E_iK_h,\qquad K_hF_i-q^{-\langle\alpha_i,h\rangle}F_iK_h\qquad(h\in P^{\vee},\ i\in I);$$

$$E_iF_j-F_jE_i-\delta_{ij}\frac{K_i-K_i^{-1}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}}\qquad(i,j\in I);$$

$$\mathrm{Serre}^+_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iE_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}E_jE_i^r,\qquad \mathrm{Serre}^-_{ij}:=\sum_{r=0}^{1-a_{ij}}(-1)^r\binom{1-a_{ij}}{r}_iF_i^{1-a_{ij}-r}F_jF_i^r\qquad(i\ne j),$$

where the Gaussian binomials are those of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. The **Drinfeld-Jimbo quantized enveloping algebra** is

$$U_q(\mathfrak g):=T/I_{\mathrm{DJ}}$$

([[def-quotient-ring]]), with $E_i,F_i,K_h$ denoting the images of the generators. In this quotient, $K_i^{-1}$ is the two-sided inverse of $K_i$.

It is graded by the root lattice $Q=\bigoplus_{i\in I}\mathbb Z\alpha_i$ ([[def-kac-moody-root-lattice-height-and-positive-cone]]), with $\deg E_i=\alpha_i$, $\deg F_i=-\alpha_i$ and $\deg K_h=0$; thus $U_q(\mathfrak g)=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$.

For every unital associative $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $B$, any assignment of elements $E_i',F_i',K_h'\in B$ satisfying these relations extends uniquely to a $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra homomorphism $U_q(\mathfrak g)\to B$ ([[thm-quotient-ring-universal-property]]).

(b) **Torus.** Write $H_i:=T_{i,0,1}$ and let $L=\sum_i\mathbb Z(d_ih_i)$.
Then $U_R^0$ has the $R$-basis
$\{K_c\prod_iK_i^{\delta_i}H_i^{t_i}\}$ with $\delta_i\in\{0,1\}$,
$t_i\ge0$ and $c$ running through the explicit representatives of
$P^{\vee}/L$ of
[[lem-unmodified-integral-torus-has-a-quantum-binomial-basis]](b); and
multiplication
$U_R^-\otimes_RU_R^0\otimes_RU_R^+\to U_R$ is an isomorphism of
$R$-modules.

(c) **Positive quotient.** For every characteristic-zero field $k$ (an
$A$-algebra via $q\mapsto1$), the positive toral quotient
$U_A^0\otimes_Ak/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is the polynomial algebra $k[H_i:i\in I]$
with, in it, $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$; and the positive full quotient
$(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1:h\in P^{\vee})$ is isomorphic to $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$,
where $\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}}$ is the classical Lie algebra presented by the
generators $e_i,f_i,h_i$ with the Cartan and Serre relations, its Cartan being
the span of the independent simple coroots. This is an assertion about the
stated quotient only: it is not claimed that $K_h=1$ in the unquotiented
specialization $U_A\otimes_Ak$, where genuine toral characters such as
$K=-1$ for $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ survive. Direct substitution $q=1$ into the
vanishing denominators $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never performed.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group
with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), with root lattice $Q$,
simple roots $\alpha_i\in P$ and integer pairing
$\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle:P\times P^{\vee}\to\mathbb Z$, and let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra with generators $E_i,F_i,K_h$
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]). The lattice $P$ plays
the role of the integral weights of the classical theory
([[def-kac-moody-integral-and-dominant-integral-weights]]); the pairing need not
be perfect, and no identification $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$ is
assumed anywhere.

A **$P$-graded type-one quantum weight module** is a left $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module $M$
together with a direct sum decomposition

$$M=\bigoplus_{\mu\in P}M_\mu$$

(an internal direct sum of $\mathbb Q(q)$-subspaces, only finitely many nonzero
on each vector) such that, for all $\mu\in P$, $h\in P^{\vee}$ and $i\in I$,

$$K_h\ \text{acts on}\ M_\mu\ \text{by the scalar}\ q^{\langle\mu,h\rangle},\qquad E_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu+\alpha_i},\qquad F_iM_\mu\subseteq M_{\mu-\alpha_i}.$$

The subspaces $M_\mu$ are the **chosen label-weight spaces**: the grading is
part of the structure and is not reconstructed from the action, because the
pairing may have a kernel. **Morphisms** of $P$-graded type-one weight modules
are the $U_q(\mathfrak g)$-module maps $f\colon M\to N$ with
$f(M_\mu)\subseteq N_\mu$ for every $\mu$; the weight submodules and quotients
considered on this page are those with the induced grading (Verification, step 2.2).

The module is **integrable** if $E_i$ and $F_i$ are locally nilpotent on every
vector: for every $v\in M$ and every $i$ there are integers $N_e(v,i),N_f(v,i)\ge1$
with $E_i^{N_e(v,i)}v=0$ and $F_i^{N_f(v,i)}v=0$. The exponents may depend on
the vector and on $i$, and both directions are required independently;
integrability is not a uniform nilpotence condition.

The following are additional hypotheses, never part of the definition:
finiteness of the dimension of every $M_\mu$; boundedness of the set of $\mu$
with $M_\mu\ne0$ above (or below); finite generation of $M$. The zero module is
a $P$-graded type-one weight module with the empty grading ($M_\mu=0$ for all
$\mu$), and it is integrable.

Two remarks are recorded here and proved below. First, when the pairing
separates $P$, the spaces $M_\mu$ are exactly the simultaneous eigenspaces of
the $K_h$, and the present definition recovers the usual type-one weight
modules (Verification, steps 2.1 and 4.1). Second, when the pairing does not
separate, distinct labels $\mu\ne\mu'$ may carry the same toral character, and
a simultaneous toral eigenspace must not be equated with a single label space;
the definition therefore takes the label grading as data. The regularization of
finite-cone support and all highest-weight comparisons on this page are proved
later, not assumed here by writing $P=\operatorname{Hom}(P^{\vee},\mathbb Z)$.
No choice principle enters this definition.

derivations.claim: Halves and positive toral quotient. By [F1], localizing at $R$ makes every $[r]_i!$ a unit, so each half is generated by its ordinary generators; the finite free components have $q=1$ fibres isomorphic to the classical halves, and the positive toral quotient is $k[H_i]$ with $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$ and the stated exact kernel. Since $k$ is an $A$-algebra through $A\to R\to k$, base change along $A\to k$ factors through $R$ and gives (a) and the toral part of (b).

The full positive quotient. By [F1] the multiplication map over $R$ is an isomorphism, so after $\otimes_Rk$ the quotient $(U_A\otimes_Ak)/(K_h-1)$ has the vector-space decomposition $U(\mathfrak n^-)_k\otimes_kk[H_i]\otimes_kU(\mathfrak n^+)_k$; by [F2] the specialized relations give an isomorphism with $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$. In this isomorphism $\bar H_i=\bar T_{i,0,1}$ corresponds to the classical coroot generator $h_i$, and $\bar T_{i,c,t}=\binom{H_i+c}{t}$; the kernel of the toral projection is exactly the ideal generated by the $K_h-1$. This proves (b).

Operator form on graded lattices. Part (c) is [F4]: the specializations of $K_h$ and $T_{i,c,t}$ on a $U_A$-stable label-graded lattice are the identity and the integer binomial scalars, and the mixed, Cartan and Serre relations hold as operator identities by reducing the integral relations; no freeness beyond the lattice's own graded structure is needed.

Boundaries. The unquotiented specialization is strictly bigger than the positive quotient in general: the $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ witness of [F6] has $K$ acting by $-1$ after $q=1$, so it cannot factor through the quotient by $K-1$, and in particular the unquotiented specialization is not identified with $U(\mathfrak g_{\mathrm{der}})_k$. Extra Cartan directions of a regular realization act diagonally on label-graded modules through the labels ([F4]); they are not added as new algebra generators of the toral integral form, whose generators are the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$ only. All divisions in the argument were performed inside $R$ on units; a vanishing denominator $q_i^s-q_i^{-s}$ is never substituted by $q=1$. This completes (d) and the proposition.

boundaries.evidence: the classical half U(n^-)_k contains the empty monomial 1, matched by the empty word in U_A^- in step 1.1; the positive quotient of step 1.2 includes the unit of k[H_i].

step 2.1 keeps the unquotiented specialization honest: the sl2 assignment E=F=0, K=-1 is nonzero on K-1, so the quotient by (K_h-1) is not the zero map on toral characters, and the specialized lattice operators of step 1.3 are genuine.
step 1.1 identifies the q=1 fibre of each half with the classical half by sending F_i to f_i and E_i to e_i, the degree-one generators; step 1.3 records Kbar_h=id on a U_A-stable graded lattice.
step 2.1 treats the degenerate unquotiented case explicitly, including extra Cartan directions of a regular realization acting diagonally, and refuses any identification beyond the stated quotient.
step 1.2 compares the two ends of the triangular decomposition over R (halves from step 1.1, torus from step 2.1's quotient), assembling U(g_der)_k degree by degree in step 1.2.

boundaries.reason: the proof assembles three earlier supplier statements and a descent to lattice operators; no family is selected, and AC is inherited only where the cited rational-local theorem declares it.
the proposition asserts isomorphisms and operator identifications, not an equivalence; parts (a) through (c) are independent claims with a boundary section (d).
no converse is asserted; step 2.1 is explicitly a warning that nothing is claimed about the unquotiented specialization, so there is no reverse implication to test.

Corrected Berkeley background to Theorem 13.2.1.10 p.317 rather than attributing the local DVR argument to it. Read Statement/Facts/Verification 1.1–2.1 with all ten dependency interfaces and the full rational-local and graded-lattice suppliers. A->k at q=1 factors through R; halves specialize componentwise, and the central K_h augmentation ideal yields the exact positive full quotient. On an arbitrary stable label-graded lattice, diagonal Laurent scalars specialize without freeness, and the integral Serre identities reduce coefficientwise. K=-1 remains a valid unquotiented rank-one character, showing why augmentation is required; extra Cartan directions are module label actions rather than fabricated integral generators. Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum group ([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]) and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. For $m\in\mathbb N$, define the **$q_i$-integer**

$$[m]_i:=\frac{q_i^m-q_i^{-m}}{q_i-q_i^{-1}},\qquad [0]_i:=0,$$

and the **$q_i$-factorial**

$$[m]_i!:=\prod_{k=1}^m[k]_i,\qquad [0]_i!:=1.$$

For $0\le r\le m$, define the **Gaussian binomial** $\binom{m}{r}_i:=[m]_i!/([r]_i![m-r]_i!)$, and set it to $0$ when $r<0$ or $r>m$. In the published one-parameter convention, write $\binom{m}{r}_t:=\binom{m}{r,m-r}_t$ for the two-part $q$-multinomial coefficient of [[def-q-integer-q-factorial-and-q-multinomial]].

For an element $x$ of a unital $\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra and $m\ge0$, define its **divided power at $q_i$** by $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$, so $x^{(0)}=1$ and $x^{(1)}=x$.

The symmetric convention and the published asymmetric convention are related, for $m\ge0$ and $0\le r\le m$, by

$$[m]_i=q_i^{-(m-1)}[m]_{q_i^2},\qquad \binom{m}{r}_i=q_i^{-r(m-r)}\binom{m}{r}_{q_i^2}.$$

In particular $[m]_i$ is invariant under $q_i\mapsto q_i^{-1}$. These quantities depend on the symmetrizer only through $q_i=q^{d_i}$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Fix a symmetrizable Cartan datum $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$, an index $i\in I$, and put $q_i=q^{d_i}$. Let $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be the Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra and let $A_i$ be the subalgebra generated by $E_i,F_i,K_i^{\pm1}$ ([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]], [[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]); write $x^{(m)}:=x^m/[m]_i!$ for the divided powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]].

(i) The assignment $e\mapsto E_i$, $f\mapsto F_i$, $k\mapsto K_i$, $k^{-1}\mapsto K_i^{-1}$ defines an algebra isomorphism from the standard rank-one algebra $\mathbb A$ over $\mathbb Q(q)$, presented by $e,f,k^{\pm1}$ with $kek^{-1}=q_i^2e$, $kfk^{-1}=q_i^{-2}f$ and $[e,f]=(k-k^{-1})/(q_i-q_i^{-1})$ onto $A_i$; the images of the monomials $F_i^aK_i^mE_i^b$ ($a,b\ge0$, $m\in\mathbb Z$) are linearly independent in $U_q(\mathfrak g)$, being images of the PBW monomials of the triangular decomposition ([[thm-triangular-decomposition-of-a-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]).

(ii) For all $a,b\ge0$, $K_iE_i^{(a)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{2a}E_i^{(a)}$ and $K_iF_i^{(b)}K_i^{-1}=q_i^{-2b}F_i^{(b)}$, and for $b\ge1$ the divided powers satisfy the exact commutation formula
$$E_iF_i^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}E_i+\frac{F_i^{(b-1)}}{q_i^{b}-q_i^{-b}}\sum_{s=0}^{b-1}\bigl(q_i^{-2s}K_i-q_i^{2s}K_i^{-1}\bigr);$$
iterating it computes $E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}$ as a finite sum of monomials $F_i^{(b-t)}K_i^{m}E_i^{(a-t)}$ ($0\le t\le\min(a,b)$) with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$.

(iii) For every $N\ge0$ there is a simple $A_i$-module $L_i(N)$ of dimension $N+1$: it is the quotient of the cyclic module $\widetilde M(N):=A_i/\bigl(A_iE_i+A_i(K_i-q_i^N)\bigr)$ by the submodule generated by $F_i^{(N+1)}w_N$, where $w_N$ is the image of $1$, with basis the images $v_t$ of $F_i^{(t)}w_N$, $0\le t\le N$, on which $K_iv_t=q_i^{N-2t}v_t$, $F_iv_t=[t+1]_iv_{t+1}$ and $E_iv_t=[N-t+1]_iv_{t-1}$ (with $v_{-1}=v_{N+1}=0$); $L_i(N)$ is the unique simple $A_i$-module generated by a vector $v\ne0$ with $E_iv=0$, $K_iv=q_i^Nv$ and $F_i^{N+1}v=0$.

Let $i\in I$ and let $T_{i,c,t}$ be the toral quantum binomials of
[[def-lusztig-divided-power-integral-form]]
($i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$, $t\ge0$, $T_{i,c,0}=1$), inside the Drinfeld–Jimbo
algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ of [[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]
with $U_A$ and its parts $U_A^-,U_A^0,U_A^+$ as in that definition. Write
$E=E_i$, $F=F_i$, $E^{(a)}=E_i^{(a)}$, $F^{(b)}=F_i^{(b)}$ for the divided
powers of [[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]] and put
$q=q_i$ inside the displayed formulas.

(i) **Divided-power multiplication.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E^{(a)}E^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iE^{(a+b)},\qquad F^{(a)}F^{(b)}=\binom{a+b}{a}_iF^{(a+b)}.$$

(ii) **Toral recursion and commutation.** For $t\ge1$,
$$T_{i,c,t}=\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-t+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+t-1}}{q_i^{\,t}-q_i^{\,-t}}\,T_{i,c,t-1}.$$
Each $T_{i,c,t}$ is a Laurent polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in
$\mathbb Q(q)$; the toral elements commute with one another and with all $K_h$.
For all $i,j$ and all $m\in\mathbb Z$ one has
$K_i^{\,m}T_{j,c,t}=T_{j,c,t}K_i^{\,m}$ if $i\ne j$, while
$E_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-2,t}E_i$, $E_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c-a_{ij},t}E_j$,
$F_iT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+2,t}F_i$, $F_jT_{i,c,t}=T_{i,c+a_{ij},t}F_j$ for all $j$.
In particular $E_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0E_i$, $F_iT_{i,c,t}\in U_A^0F_i$,
$T_{i,c,t}E_i=E_iT_{i,c+2,t}\in E_iU_A^0$ and
$T_{i,c,t}F_i=F_iT_{i,c-2,t}\in F_iU_A^0$: the toral factor can be moved to the
middle at the cost of a shift of the binomial index.

(iii) **Reordering identity.** For all $a,b\ge0$,
$$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(b)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(a,b)}F_i^{(b-t)}\,T_{i,\,2t-a-b,\,t}\,E_i^{(a-t)},$$
with every coefficient a toral quantum binomial in $U_A^0$. In particular
$E_iF_i-F_iE_i=T_{i,0,1}$ and
$E_i^{(a)}F_i^{(a)}=\sum_{t=0}^{a}F_i^{(a-t)}T_{i,2t-2a,t}E_i^{(a-t)}$.
For $i\ne j$, $E_i^{(a)}$ and $F_j^{(b)}$ commute; the same-half divided powers
$E_i^{(a)},E_j^{(b)}$ (and likewise $F_i^{(a)},F_j^{(b)}$) commute whenever
$a_{ij}=0$, and for $a_{ij}\ne0$ no commutation is asserted.

(iv) **Triangular spanning.** Every element of $U_A$ is an $A$-linear
combination of products $b_-u\,b_+$ with $b_-\in U_A^-$, $u\in U_A^0$ and
$b_+\in U_A^+$; equivalently $U_A=U_A^-U_A^0U_A^+$ as an $A$-module. No
independence of the spanning family is asserted.

Let $(I,A,D,P,P^{\vee},q)$ be a symmetrizable Cartan datum for a quantum
group with $a_{ii}=2$ for all $i$
([[def-symmetrizable-cartan-datum-for-a-quantum-group]]), let
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ be its Drinfeld–Jimbo algebra
([[def-drinfeld-jimbo-quantized-enveloping-algebra]]) with $q_i=q^{d_i}$ and
$K_i=K_{d_ih_i}$, and set

$$A:=\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]\ \subseteq\ \mathbb Q(q),$$

the image of the Laurent polynomial ring $\Lambda_1=\mathbb Z[t]_{S}$ of
[[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]] under the unital ring homomorphism sending
$t$ to the indeterminate $q$; this homomorphism is injective and $A$ is a
subring of $\mathbb Q(q)$ (Verification, step 1.1). We work over this
commutative domain $A$ inside the field $\mathbb Q(q)$.

For $i\in I$, $c\in\mathbb Z$ and $t\ge0$ define the **toral quantum binomial**

$$T_{i,c,t}:=\begin{bmatrix}K_i;c\\ t\end{bmatrix}:=\prod_{s=1}^{t}\frac{K_iq_i^{\,c-s+1}-K_i^{-1}q_i^{\,-c+s-1}}{q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}}\in U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

the empty product being $T_{i,c,0}:=1$. Each factor is defined in
$U_q(\mathfrak g)$ because $q_i^{\,s}-q_i^{\,-s}\ne0$ for $s\ge1$
([[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]), so
$T_{i,c,t}$ is a polynomial in $K_i^{\pm1}$ with coefficients in $\mathbb Q(q)$;
in particular all $T_{i,c,t}$ commute with the $K_h$ and with one another
(Verification, step 2.1).

The **Lusztig divided-power integral form** is the $A$-subalgebra

$$U_A:=\bigl\langle E_i^{(r)},\ F_i^{(r)},\ K_h^{\pm1},\ T_{i,c,t}\ \colon\ i\in I,\ r,t\ge0,\ c\in\mathbb Z,\ h\in P^{\vee}\bigr\rangle\ \subseteq\ U_q(\mathfrak g),$$

where $x^{(r)}=x^r/[r]_i!$ are the divided powers of
[[def-quantum-integers-factorials-and-divided-powers-at-q-i]]. Write $U_A^\pm$
for the $A$-subalgebras generated by the $E_i^{(r)}$ and by the $F_i^{(r)}$,
and $U_A^0$ for the one generated by the $K_h^{\pm1}$ and the $T_{i,c,t}$.

Then:

(i) $U_A$ contains $E_i=E_i^{(1)}$, $F_i=F_i^{(1)}$ and all $K_h$;

(ii) $U_A$ is a root-graded $A$-subalgebra of the root-graded
$\mathbb Q(q)$-algebra $U_q(\mathfrak g)$ ([[def-positive-negative-and-toral-quantum-subalgebras]]):
with $U_A[\beta]:=U_A\cap U_q(\mathfrak g)[\beta]$ one has
$U_A=\bigoplus_{\beta\in Q}U_A[\beta]$, each $U_A[\beta]$ is an $A$-submodule,
and $U_A^\pm,U_A^0$ are graded in the same way;

(iii) $U_A\otimes_A\mathbb Q(q)\cong U_q(\mathfrak g)$ canonically, i.e. the
$\mathbb Q(q)$-span of $U_A$ is all of $U_q(\mathfrak g)$.

The shifted binomials $T_{i,c,t}$ with $c\ne0$ are included because the
divided-power reordering identity of
[[lem-divided-power-and-toral-quantum-binomial-reordering-identities]] has
coefficients $T_{i,2t-a-b,t}$ with a nonconstant index; the specializations at
$q=1$ of these elements are computed in
[[lem-q-one-toral-specialization-identifies-the-classical-cartan-generators]],
and the integral triangular decomposition and the specialization are treated
only after this definition.

No freeness of $U_A$ or of its parts over $A$, no independence of the listed
generators, and no triangularity of the products of the three parts is asserted
here. In particular $A$ is not a principal ideal domain (Verification, step
7.1), so no torsion-free-to-free inference over $A$ is permitted anywhere on
this page.
